scaffold a new tool\n    ├── check_audit_ignores.py  # pip-audit suppression guard (+ audit/ config)\n    ├── check_tool_wiring.py    # pre-commit tool-wiring check\n    ├── parity_brief_portfolio.py\n    └── gen_zettel_writer_fixtures.py\n```\n\n**Key patterns:**\n\n- **Single package**: `buvis-gems` on PyPI, one `uv tool install`\n- **Namespace package**: `src/lib/buvis/` has no `__init__.py`\n- **Hatch packages**: each `src/tools/<name>/` maps to top-level `<name>` in wheel\n- **Libraries are internal**: pybase + zettel not published separately\n- **All-interface rule**: every command/action must work across CLI, TUI, API, and WebUI\n\n## Tool Structure\n\nEvery tool under `src/tools/<name>/` follows a base layout:\n\n```text\ntool_name/\n├── __init__.py\n├── __main__.py\n├── cli.py              # Click entry point\n├── settings.py         # Tool-specific settings\n└── commands/           # One module per CLI command\n```\n\nAdd subdirs only when needed:\n\n| Dir | When | Example |\n|-----|------|---------|\n| `adapters/` | External service clients | fctracker, readerctl |\n| `domain/` | Business logic beyond simple commands | fctracker |\n| `shared/` | Code reused across commands | zseq |\n\n> `bim/commands/serve/frontend/` contains the WebUI SvelteKit app — the only tool with a frontend subtree.\n\n> `bim/commands/doc/` follows the existing `commands/serve/`-style group pattern with a `shared/` subdir holding cross-command utilities (pipeline, OCR/classifier/extractor adapters, state DB, issuer registry, zettel writer).\n\n## Code Conventions\n\n**Type hints** — modern style, no `Optional`:\n\n```python\nfrom __future__ import annotations\ndef foo(path: Path | None = None) -> list[str]: ...\n```\n\n**Imports**:\n\n- Explicit `__all__` in `__init__.py`\n- `TYPE_CHECKING` guards for type-only imports\n\n**Docstrings**: Google format\n\n**CLI pattern**: Click-based. `buvis_options` adds `--version`, `--config`, `--log-level`, `--debug`, and `--update` to every tool automatically:\n\n```python\n@click.command()\n@buvis_options\n@click.pass_context\ndef cli(ctx: click.Context) -> None:\n    settings = get_settings(ctx)\n    ...\n```\n\n**Lazy imports in CLI handlers**: import command classes inside handler functions, not at module level. This avoids pulling in optional/heavy dependencies before the user picks a subcommand:\n\n```python\n@cli.command(\"create\")\n@click.pass_context\ndef create(ctx):\n    from bim.commands.create_note.create_note import CommandCreateNote\n    ...\n```\n\n## Error Handling\n\n**Command layer** (`commands/`):\n- Return `CommandResult` for all outcomes — success and failure\n- Catch expected exceptions (e.g. `FileNotFoundError`) internally, return `CommandResult(success=False, error=str(exc))`\n- No `console.panic()` or `sys.exit()` inside command classes\n- No custom exception classes for control flow\n\n**CLI layer** (`cli.py`):\n- Inspect `CommandResult` and call `console.panic()` / `console.failure()` / `console.success()`\n- Use `console.report_result()` for standardized output\n- Catch `ImportError` for optional deps, call `console.require_import()`\n- Catch `FatalError` for unrecoverable infrastructure failures\n\n**Click argument validation**:\n- Avoid parse-time validators that short-circuit before the callback (`click.Path(exists=True)`, `IntRange`, custom `ParamType.convert` that raises). They emit Click's default `Usage: ... Error: ...` formatting and bypass the buvis console.\n- Validate inside the callback instead: `if not path.is_file(): console.panic(f\"file not found: {path}\"); return`.\n- `click.Choice` is the exception — its parse-time error lists the valid values, which is more useful than a rewritten message.\n\n**Console methods**:\n- Fatal (exit): `console.panic(msg)` — prints + exits with code 1\n- Recoverable: `console.failure(msg)` — prints, continues\n- Status: `console.success()`, `console.warning()`, `console.info()`\n- All user-facing output must route through `console`. No `print()`, `sys.stdout.write()`, `sys.stderr.write()`, `click.echo()`, `click.secho()`, or the Python logging module. Plain writes bypass the buvis prefix markers (`✘`, `✓`, etc.) and become indistinguishable from stray output, which is what makes a missed `console.panic` look like a print statement to the user.\n- The one sanctioned exception is the `dot filter` clean/smudge plumbing, which writes git's blob payload as raw bytes on stdout and at most one error line on stderr, because git owns both streams and a console marker would corrupt the payload (discovery R12).\n- Never let raw exceptions (stack traces) reach the user.\n\n## Invariants (evolution guardrails)\n\nThese encode the failure classes surfaced by the 2026-07-09 evolution assessment (`docs/dev/project-management/reviews/evolution-assessment-2026-07-09.md`). Force locally with `BUVIS_SNAPSHOT_CANONICAL=1` only if you know what you're doing.\n\n## Installation\n\n```bash\nuv tool install buvis-gems              # core only (no tool-specific deps)\nuv tool install buvis-gems[bim]         # with jira support\nuv tool install buvis-gems[bim-web]     # bim web UI deps\nuv tool install buvis-gems[all]         # everything\nuv tool upgrade buvis-gems              # update\n```\n\nExtras: `bim`, `bim-web`, `doc`, `dot`, `fren`, `morph`, `muc`, `pinger`, `postup`, `postup-web`, `readerctl`, `all`\n\n## Release\n\n> Full procedure (version authority, checks, destinations, partial-failure recovery): `docs/dev/procedures/releasing.md`.\n\n```bash\nrelease patch|minor|major              # bump, tag, push → CI publishes to PyPI\nrelease --pre rc1                      # pre-release current version to TestPyPI\nrelease --pre rc1 minor                # bump + pre-release to TestPyPI\nrelease                                # after rc: strip suffix, release stable to PyPI\nrelease local                          # build .devN wheel + install locally\nrelease --dry-run [--pre rc1] [patch]  # preview without changes\n```\n\n`mise` adds `tools` to PATH (shims; `tools/lib` holds the implementations). Other provider hosts use their host mapping.\n\n# Autopilot\n\nOrchestrate the full PRD lifecycle: catchup → design → plan-tasks → work → review-rework loop (consensus + blind + doubt lenses, every cycle) → done.\n\nMakes autonomous decisions backed by research (dependencies, recurring issues, API/schema changes when PRD-driven) and pauses only for critical security, requirements ambiguity, or blocking decisions.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- Pack skills (invoked as phases): `design-solution`, `plan-tasks`, `work`,\n  `review-work-completion`\n- Plugin skills: `git-ferry:catchup` (Phase 1, unless the PRD sets `catchup: skip`)\n- Files read from other skill dirs:\n  `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/review-work-completion/scripts/await_reviewer_outputs.py`\n  (Watcher keep-alive)\n- Hooks outside the skill dir: `~/.claude/hooks/notify.py`\n- Shell wrapper outside `~/.claude`: `autoclaude` in\n  `~/.config/bash/plugins/development.plugin.bash` - operator subcommands +\n  tracon front-end; it hands off to `autopilot loop` (`cli/loop.py`), the\n  unattended session loop since PRD 00106\n- Scripts (own dir, model-invoked as a CLI): `scripts/statectl.py` — the sole\n  `state.json` mutator (`get`/`set`/`append`/`del`; atomic, advisory-locked,\n  one rotating `.bak`)\n- CLIs: `claude` (headless `-p`), `python3` (>= 3.11), `git`, `awk`\n- Optional: `tracon` (`scripts/tracon/`; the default `autoclaude` front-end since PRD 00062, `_AUTOPILOT_TRACON=0` or no tty/`uv` falls back to `render_stream.py`) - dashboard only, absence changes nothing\n\n## Execution Model\n\n**Run all phases in sequence without stopping.** After each phase completes, immediately update state and proceed to the next phase. Do not pause between phases, do not summarize progress, do not wait for user input - unless the phase explicitly says PAUSE or STOP. Completing a sub-skill invocation (`/git-ferry:catchup`, `/autopilot:plan-tasks`, `/autopilot:work`, `/autopilot:review-work-completion`, etc.) is NOT a stopping point. It is an intermediate step. Continue.\n\nReview sessions run on opus at xhigh in cycle 1 and at high on cycle 2 and later; _AUTOPILOT_EFFORT_REVIEW forces one effort for every cycle and _AUTOPILOT_EFFORT_REVIEW_RERUN sets the rerun value. A rework resume (the cycle's review file exists and `rework_task_ids` names an unfinished task) runs on the queued tasks' own tier instead, sonnet unless one is opus or fable (`references/model-ladder.md` § Review sessions, PRD 00207).\n\n## Entry Points\n\n- `/autopilot:run-autopilot` — auto-select PRD (wip first, then backlog), run full cycle\n- `/autopilot:run-autopilot <prd-filename>` — full cycle with specific PRD\n- `/autopilot:run-autopilot status` — print current dashboard, no action\n- `/autopilot:run-autopilot review-batch` — interactively review a finished batch's deferred items\n\nIf invoked with `status`, read `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json`, print phase/cycle/task summary, and stop.\n\nIf invoked with `review-batch`, load the newest `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/deferred/{batch_id}-deferred.json` and run the \"Batch-End Review\" presentation (`references/phase-done.md`) against it — chunked by PRD, wait for user decisions, execute \"fix now\" items. After the entry-point checks, read `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json` and **Read the matching gate file now; do not execute a gate from memory**:\n\nA state carrying `stall_op` runs `autopilot park` to reconcile before any gate file is read.\n\n| resume state | Read this gate file |\n|--------------|---------------------|\n| `phase: \"build\"` — or `state.json` missing (fresh start) | `references/phase-build.md` |\n| `phase: \"review\"` — or a legacy `\"blind\"`/`\"doubt\"` value (pre-00015 state), which maps to `review` | `references/phase-review.md` |\n| `phase: \"done\"` | `references/phase-done.md` |\n| `phase: \"paused\"` — or `stall_reason` set | `references/phase-build.md` (its Phase 0 abort/pause handlers own this resume) |\n\n`status` and `review-batch` invocations do not dispatch a gate (see Entry Points).\n\n## State Management\n\nAll autopilot artifacts live under `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/`, organized by type:\n\n```\ndocs/dev/project-management/autopilot/\n  state.json                              # current cycle state\n  last-session.log                        # loop-teed raw output of the last headless session\n  reports/{batch_id}-report.md            # batch audit report\n  deferred/{batch_id}-deferred.json       # unresolved items across PRDs\n```\n\nState file: `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json` — see `references/state-schema.md` for schema.\n\n**`statectl` is the sole writer of `state.json`.** Apply every field mutation with `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/scripts/statectl.py <state.json> set|append|del <json-path> <json-value>` (read one field with `get`); it takes an advisory lock, backs up to `<state.json>.bak`, changes only the named path while preserving all siblings, and replaces the file atomically — so it cannot leave a half-written or unparseable state, and it never trips the \"not read yet\" / \"modified since read\" errors the editing tools hit. Since PRD 00089 it is a shim over `cli/state.transaction`, so every write is schema-validated too: a value that is malformed **for the field it targets** is rejected with exit 1 and the file left byte-unchanged (an unrelated pre-existing odd field blocks nothing). **Phase transitions are not field mutations** — use `autopilot phase-done --outcome <outcome>` (§ Session handoff procedure), never a hand-written `set phase` / `set next_phase` pair, so a transition cannot land without the effects it mandates. Resolve `<state.json>` by walking up from the resolved physical cwd to the autopilot dir (the `_walk_up.py` pattern in `/autopilot:work` step 2). The terse `set X` / `write field Y` / per-PRD-reset instructions throughout these skills and the gate files name the fields to change; each is applied with `statectl`, never by hand-editing the file.\n\nDocumented human fallback: outside the loop a person may still Edit or Write `state.json` by hand (for forensics or recovery — the model itself never hand-edits `state.json`; a statectl failure has its own marker-based recovery below); `validate_state_json_hook.py` catches a hand-edit that leaves the file unparseable and now also runs `cli.schema.validate` on it, and `statectl` reads whatever valid JSON it finds on its next mutation.\n\n**When `statectl` itself fails** (nonzero exit — advisory-lock contention, a Python error, an unreadable `state.json`): retry the exact command ONCE. If it fails again, do NOT improvise a partial write and do NOT proceed on the stale state — a lost mutation strands the loop on the wrong `next_phase`. Run `autopilot restore` (rolls `state.json` back to `<state.json>.bak`) and retry the statectl command once more. If the failure persists (`autopilot restore` itself fails, or the subsequent statectl write still fails), WRITE THE MARKER `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state-write-failed` with the Write tool — ONE line of JSON `{\"site\": \"statectl_fail\", \"detail\": \"<the statectl command and its raw stderr>\"}` — and END THE TURN: the wrapper halts on the marker and surfaces the `detail` itself, so no further state write is needed. Interactive sessions ALSO report the same failure to the user directly (there is no wrapper watching an interactive terminal). The raw stderr rides into the marker's `detail` so the failure is diagnosable, never silent (`rules/operating-principles.md`). (Lock contention on the single-writer model implies a second loop or a stale lock; the concurrent-loop guard below now refuses a second loop up front, so a persistent lock is a stale one — the retry clears it or the marker records it.)\n\nCreate `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/` and subdirectories if missing. Initialize state file at PRD selection. Update state at every phase transition. Autopilot also keeps a per-PRD **decision audit log** at `docs/dev/project-management/reviews/<prd-base>-audit.md`, **rendered once at Phase 9 finalize from the `state.json` decision arrays** (`autonomous_decisions`, `deferred_decisions`, `doubts`). `state.json` is the single in-run source of truth — decisions are NOT mirrored to `audit.md` incrementally per decision. Each rendered entry carries a **source** label (`autonomous`, `deferred`, or `doubt`); cycle/phase context goes in the entry body so the Phase 9 `decisions.md` projection can filter autonomous entries by label. The three gates are `build` | `review` | `done` (plus `paused`). `build` is ONE session: selection, catchup, design, planning, and work all run under `phase: \"build\"` with no mid-build handoff. The review surface runs in its own fresh session; blind and doubt scrutiny are LENSES inside every review cycle (Blake and Bob in `review-work-completion`'s roster), not separate phases — reviewers get isolated contexts by construction (subagent prompts, external CLIs). The authoritative resume signal is `phase` + `phases_completed`; build sub-step skipping is by ARTIFACT (capsule freshness, design-doc-exists, tasks-exist, all-done), not by `phases_completed` membership. This resume decision (phase + phases_completed + artifact checks → next step) is encoded canonically in `cli/resume.py` (`scripts/resume_target.py` re-exports it), which `scripts/test_autopilot_resume.py` imports — editing the resume logic there flips a test red rather than silently drifting from this prose. Run `autopilot resume-target` at Phase 0 to print what that encoding says the next action is, and reconcile it against the handler you are about to follow: a disagreement means the prose and the encoded contract have drifted, and the encoding wins. It answers for the `build` and `review` gates; `phase: \"done\"` returns `unknown phase: done` by design — the done gate is routed by the table above, not by this function.\n\n### Retention\n\nEverything under `docs/dev/project-management/` is tracked work-management state. a test keeps the two in step.\n\nTemporary review context and other reproducible scratch material belongs under the globally ignored `docs/dev/tmp/` tree. `purge-devtmp` operates only there, preserves files linked to live PRDs, and never traverses `docs/dev/project-management/`.\n\nBatch end and cleanup steps enumerate lifecycle-owned runtime files explicitly; they never remove a directory wholesale. This keeps a completed PRD's complete review trail intact after the batch closes (`references/design-rationale.md` § Verified moves).\n\n### Resuming\n\nWhen `/autopilot:run-autopilot` is invoked and `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json` exists with `batch.completed_prds`, this is a continuation after a session restart. Preserve `batch.completed_prds` (including `batch.id`) and proceed to the build gate's Phase 0 to pick the next PRD.\n\nDelete `state.pause_reason` from `state.json` if present — unconditional, on every invocation, NOT gated on `batch.completed_prds`. A new session means any pause is being resumed; `pause_reason` belongs only to an unresolved pause and is not overwritten by normal progression, so it must be cleared here or it halts the resumed PRD's next hand-off. Cap-pause detection is unaffected — it keys on `cap_pause_reason`, which this delete does not touch.\n\n### Operator runbook (unattended batches)\n\nAll interaction with a running `autoclaude` batch happens at session boundaries — the only safe point. (Operator-shell commands for the human's own terminal, not for the model's Bash tool — `tail -f` would hang a session and pipes are hook-blocked.)\n\n- **Watch**: `tail -f docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/last-session.log` — the wrapper tees the live event log of the running headless turn there.\n- **Pause**: `touch docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/pause-requested` — the wrapper consumes the marker at the next session boundary, notifies \"paused by operator\", and stops the loop with state intact. It leaves `paused-by-operator` behind so tracon shows `⏸ paused` rather than `⚠ orphaned`; plain `autoclaude` resumes (nothing to clear, no decision to make). The marker may carry a JSON reason, `{\"reason\": \"...\"}`, which the stop line and the notification quote; a session that stands down for a peer writes one with a `condition` beside it, after asking the peer first (§ Session Loop, stand-down procedure).\n- **Take over**: with the loop stopped (pause marker, or Ctrl-C on the wrapper), run `/autopilot:run-autopilot` in a normal interactive session — resume-by-artifact reads the same `state.json`, and full interactive semantics (questions, PAUSEs) apply because `$_AUTOPILOT_LOOP` is unset. Restart `autoclaude` afterwards to go unattended again.\n- **Resume after a PAUSE** (`phase: \"paused\"` in `state.json`, \"session paused\" banner/ntfy): same take-over recipe, and it is the ONLY way forward — re-running `autoclaude` reads the paused state and exits again immediately. Interactively, the phase that paused re-runs with `AskUserQuestion` available, so the blockers that halted the loop are asked as decisions instead. Answer them, let the session hand off or finish the PRD, then re-run `autoclaude`.\n- **Un-park a sidelined PRD**: a PRD the loop parked (a `wrapper_died` death-park, or a loop-mode `design_gate` / `blocking_escalation` stall) sits in `docs/dev/project-management/prds/hold/` with its stall recorded in the batch deferred JSON; the batch kept draining without it. To resume it, `mv docs/dev/project-management/prds/hold/<00XXX-…>.md docs/dev/project-management/prds/backlog/` (keep the `00XXX-` prefix). Autopilot never reads `hold/`, so the next `/autopilot:run-autopilot` (or `autoclaude` relaunch) re-selects it from `backlog/` and re-enters the build gate, reusing its existing design doc via the Phase 1.5 artifact skip (a `design_gate` park then re-fires the gate interactively). Batch-end review lists every parked PRD (`{m} stalled`), so none is silently forgotten.\n- **Forensics**: `claude --resume <session-id>` (the id is in the init event at the top of `last-session.log`) reopens a finished headless conversation for questioning. Harmless by construction: sessions are disposable; `state.json` plus the artifacts are the only orchestration contract, so a resumed chat cannot fork the loop.\n- **Run a wave (parallel lanes)**: `autopilot wave plan`, then `autopilot wave launch`, `autopilot wave status` and `autopilot wave abort` — one detached loop per lane worktree, each over its own slice of the backlog. Full operator surface, including what is deferred: `references/waves.md`.\n- **Product QA (agoge)**: once a batch drains at least one PRD, the loop runs a single product-QA pass (`/run-agoge` over the repo), logging to `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/reports/{batch}-agoge.log`. A batch that drained nothing skips it with a line saying so; a QA failure is recorded and swallowed, never turning a successful drain into a failed one. `_AUTOPILOT_AGOGE_CAP` (default 3600s) bounds a hung run.\n\n- **One loop per repo**: a second `autoclaude` on a repo that already has a live loop refuses to start, naming the incumbent loop's PID (both the tracon front-end and the plain/headless path check the loop registry via `scripts/tracon_wrapper_alive.py` before registering). This prevents two loops double-draining the backlog and racing `state.json` writes. If the refusal is wrong (the named PID is dead), the stale registry entry is pruned automatically on the next launch; force it by deleting `~/.claude/autopilot-loops/<pid>.json`.\n\nA running headless turn is interrupted by the wrapper's wall-clock cap (`_AUTOPILOT_SESSION_MAX`, default 7200s; review-phase launches use `_AUTOPILOT_SESSION_MAX_REVIEW`, default 10800s) and, independently, by the idle watchdog at any point after launch: it kills a session whose log has gone silent for `_AUTOPILOT_SESSION_IDLE` seconds (default 1200s; `0` disables pre-cap idle kill, restoring the old kill-at-cap-only behavior) as long as nothing is in flight (`session_busy`) - this fires before the cap, not only past it. Fifteen minutes before the cap (`_AUTOPILOT_SESSION_WARN`, seconds, `0` disables) the wrapper writes the same `.handoff-requested` marker the context-cap hook writes, so a session that reaches a task boundary inside that window hands off cleanly instead of being killed mid-task. Once the wall-clock cap itself is reached, the same idle-silence watchdog applies, or the session is SIGTERMed at twice the cap (the ceiling), whichever comes first.\n\nA PRD whose session metrics ledger spend since `state.prd_budget_since` exceeds `_AUTOPILOT_PRD_BUDGET_USD` (float; default 300; `0` disables; an unparseable value keeps 300) is parked (`park_site: \"budget\"`) rather than left to burn further sessions unattended.\n\nThe agoge run above arms the runtime-security lane by default, passing `--authorized autoclaude-drain`; `_AUTOPILOT_AGOGE_AUTHORIZED=0` is the kill switch, dropping just that flag so QA still runs, unarmed. Only the literal `0` disables it: anything else, including `false`, `no`, `off`, or `0` with a trailing space, leaves it armed, because a security brake should fail toward armed, not away from it. It brakes a default-on assertion; it is not a separate way to invoke one, since the assertion itself stays invocation-only.\n\n### Task Counts\n\n`tasks_total` and `tasks_completed` are maintained by whoever writes the `state.tasks` snapshot: recompute both in the same write — `tasks_total = len(tasks)`, `tasks_completed = count(status == \"completed\")` (the pidash-era PostToolUse sync hook is retired, PRD 00063). The model does not re-derive these counts by any other means; the arithmetic runs on the snapshot already in hand. Keep `state.tasks` accurate at phase transitions and recompute the counts alongside each `tasks` snapshot, applying all three with `statectl set` (§ State Management), keeping the dashboard progress bar live.\n\n### Live Dashboard\n\n`autoclaude` launches `tracon` (`scripts/tracon/`) in the foreground by default (PRD 00062), so the loop terminal shows the live dashboard with no extra step. It reads `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json` — no action needed from autopilot beyond keeping the state file updated. `q` detaches (loop keeps running, wrapper prints the reattach command), `p` pauses at the next session boundary, `Ctrl-C` stops the loop with full cleanup. When there is no tty, no `uv`, or `_AUTOPILOT_TRACON=0`, the loop terminal shows the `render_stream.py` fallback with per-lane subagent tags instead. Full operator surface: `references/dashboard-format.md`.\n\n### Phase Banners\n\nPrint a banner at each phase transition:\n\n```\n── AUTOPILOT ── PRD: {prd-name} ── Phase: {PHASE} ──────────────────\n── AUTOPILOT ── PRD: {prd-name} ── Phase: REVIEW ── Cycle {n} ─────\n── AUTOPILOT ── PRD: {prd-name} ── Cycle {n} rework complete ───────\n── AUTOPILOT ── handing off to fresh session for cycle {n+1} ───────\n── AUTOPILOT ── PAUSED ── {n} issue(s) need your decision ──────────\n── AUTOPILOT ── PRD: {prd-name} ── DONE ── {n} cycles ─────────────\n```\n\n## Session Loop\n\nUnattended mode runs each session headless: the `autoclaude` wrapper (in `~/.config/bash/plugins/development.plugin.bash`) hands off to `autopilot loop` — the CLI loop driver, `cli/loop.py` (PRD 00106) — which launches `claude -p \"/autopilot:run-autopilot\"`; the session runs exactly one turn, and the process exits at turn end. There is no signal file and no Stop-hook choreography — **`state.json` is the entire hand-off contract** (`references/design-rationale.md` § Headless sessions). For a single hand-off rather than a whole batch — the hybrid track's fresh-session review and finalize hops — run `autopilot review-once`: it runs the same preflights and one routed session for `state.next_phase`, then exits, never relaunching or parking, and refuses any phase but `review` or `done` before spawning. Export `_AUTOPILOT_WRITE_SCOPE_EXTRA` first when the project spans roots outside its repo (`~/.claude/AGENTS.md` § Toolchain), same as for a batch. Each launch passes `--strict-mcp-config --mcp-config <value>` so a loop session loads only the Context7 MCP server instead of every claude.ai connector on the account; `_AUTOPILOT_MCP_CONFIG=inherit` restores the unscoped launch, and any other value overrides the config verbatim (`mcp_config_for`, `cli/runner.py`).\n\n**Hand-off = write state, print banner, end the turn.** After the process exits, the loop driver reads `state.json` and branches:\n\n0. `state-write-failed` marker present → stop the loop and notify with its `detail`, without needing `state.json` to be readable.\n1. `pause_reason` set or `phase == \"paused\"` → notify the user with the pause detail, stop the loop, state left intact.\n2. `stall_reason.stalled == \"subagent_prompt_overrun\"` (set by `/autopilot:work`'s Subagent Dispatch Budget when an assembled subagent prompt exceeded 50K after one trim pass; `/autopilot:work` also appends to `state.task_aborts`) → continue the loop; Phase 0 of the next session replans the PRD in place (PRD stays in `wip/`; see the build gate's abort handlers). This is the one surviving replan path.\n3. `next_phase == \"\"` (empty) → backlog drained: the loop archives `state.json` to `reports/{batch_id}-state-final.json`, notifies, and stops the loop.\n4. `next_phase` non-empty → relaunch a fresh session, which resumes from state by artifact — capsule fresh → skip catchup, tasks exist → skip planning, `/autopilot:work` continues at the first non-completed task.\n5. `state.json` missing, unreadable, or untouched by the session → first a stand-down check: a `pause-requested` marker written during the session means the session found another session owning its PRD and stood down on purpose (the stand-down procedure below) — the loop consumes the marker, stamps `paused-by-operator`, notifies with the marker's reason, and stops with state intact; no retry burned, no park marker, `autoclaude` alone resumes (PRD 00172). Otherwise a usage-limit check against the captured session log (`last-session.log`; a live limit means sleep-until-reset and continue). Otherwise a genuine death: with a PRD selected (`state.prd` non-empty) the loop retries the relaunch once (`_AUTOPILOT_DIED_RETRIES_MAX`, default 1), then on exhaustion PARKS it — writes `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/park-requested` (`{prd, reason}`) and relaunches, so the next session's Phase 0 park handler sidelines the sick PRD to `hold/` and the batch keeps draining (PRD 00066). Only a **bootstrap** death (no PRD selected — nothing to park) notifies \"died\" and stops loud; an unconsumed park marker trips the loop's park-loop guard (also a loud stop; guarded relaunches back off `_AUTOPILOT_PARK_BACKOFF`, default 30s, and a marker whose write fails outright halts loud rather than handing off an empty marker). These two are rows 8 and 10 of the Error Handling § sanctioned batch-halt list.\n\nA Work-turn context-cap overrun is just branch 4: `autopilot_context_cap_hook.py` records the rotation (appends to `state.cap_rotations`, resets the in-flight task to `pending`, sets `next_phase: \"build\"`), the turn ends, and the fresh session resumes `build` by artifact — NO replan.\n\n**Stand-down procedure (a peer session owns the PRD).** A headless session never works a PRD another session is already working: two writers on one `state.json` and one set of task artifacts corrupt both, and the one-loop-per-repo guard sees only wrappers, not a bare interactive session. Phase 0 asks before it pauses. A peer counts only when `ListAgents` shows a busy interactive session whose name starts with this repository's directory basename (`basename \"$PWD\"`, e.g. `agent-skills-`); a session named for another repository is never evidence, whatever it is busy with (the two 2026-09-14 false stand-downs in agent-skills each cited a `claude-autopilot-*` session, the other repo's own loop). When such a peer exists, send it one `SendMessage` naming the PRD and wait at most 120 s for a reply. Stand down only when the reply claims the PRD (condition `peer_claimed`), or when writer evidence is present: `autopilot dirty` prints at least one path (condition `dirty_tree`; store writes never count as this evidence), or the mtime of `state.json` or `contract-card.md`, truncated to whole seconds, is greater than the `at` of the most recent `kind: \"handoff\"` row with `edge: \"leave\"` and this PRD's `prd` in `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/dispatch-metrics.jsonl` (condition `state_after_leave`; the rows carry no batch id, so the `prd` filter is what keeps an older batch's row out; when no such `leave` row exists, skip the mtime test and let the dirty-tree test and the reply decide). That comparison holds only because every handoff site writes its `leave` row AFTER its last state and card write (§ Session handoff procedure orders step 1 before step 2; `/autopilot:work`'s task-boundary handoff must set `next_phase` before its row too): a site that touches `state.json` after its row makes every next session read its own hand-off as peer evidence. To stand down: do not select, move, or write anything else; write `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/pause-requested` with the Write tool as one JSON line, `{\"reason\": \"<peer session> owns <prd> (<evidence>)\", \"condition\": \"<peer_claimed | dirty_tree | state_after_leave>\"}`, and end the turn. The loop reads a marker written during the session as a stand-down (branch 5 above): it stops with state intact, burns no retry, writes no park marker, quotes the reason in its stop line and notification, and records `stood_down` and `stood_down_condition` in the session's `loop-metrics.jsonl` row; `autoclaude` alone resumes once the peer is done. Before this procedure existed (2026-09-02, agent-skills PRD 00010) four stand-downs read as deaths and parked a healthy PRD mid-task.\n\nThe model's only job at a hand-off is to write `state.next_phase` (and `phase`/`stall_reason`) accurately, print the banner, and end the turn. Dispatched work — `Agent` calls and background Bash — returns its results **within the same headless turn**: the harness re-invokes you with each `<task-notification>` before the turn can end, so dispatch, overlap independent work, wait for the results, and finish the phase. If genuine work cannot finish in this session, that is a PAUSE (`phase: \"paused\"` + `state.pause_reason = {\"site\": \"work_incomplete\", \"detail\": \"<what could not finish>\"}` + end turn), not a silent idle stop.\n\n### Session handoff procedure (canonical — gate files invoke it by site name)\n\nEvery session handoff is the same three steps:\n\n1. **Apply the transition** with one `autopilot phase-done --outcome <outcome>` call (table below). To survive that, **at each gate transition write a compact contract card** — the current step, the active invariants, and the next gate:\n\n- **Autopilot (state.json world):** write the body to `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/contract-card.md` with the **Write tool**, then load it with one call:\n  ```bash\n  python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/scripts/statectl.py <state.json> set-contract-card docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/contract-card.md\n  ```\n  Keep it a few lines: `step: <phase/step> | invariants: <the 2-3 that bind right now> | next: <the next gate + its precondition>`. **Never pass the card as an inline shell argument** — it carries quotes, newlines and `$`, and the inline `set contract_card '<string>'` form failed three consecutive times on quoting in a real build session (2026-08-02, engram session 6).\n- **Interactive (no state.json):** the file write above is the whole step; skip the statectl call.\n\nThe session brief (`write-brief`, § Session handoff procedure step 2) is rendered right after this call so it carries the card just loaded; `/autopilot:work`'s task-boundary handoff and `/autopilot:review-work-completion`'s cycle transition write the brief the same way where they write their cards.\n\n`reinject_contract_card.py` is a SessionStart hook **matched to `compact` only** (startup/resume/clear stay unmatched, so there is no standing token cost); after a compaction it reads the card back and re-injects it as additionalContext. `/autopilot:work` (task-boundary transitions) and `/autopilot:review-work-completion` (cycle transitions) write their own cards the same way — `contract_card` in `references/state-schema.md`.\n\n### Loop Detection\n\nThe `autoclaude` wrapper exports `_AUTOPILOT_LOOP=$$` before launching each headless session.  -> consume it, notify, stop\n           spawn the routed `claude -p \"/autopilot:run-autopilot\"` (raw events kept in last-session.log)\n           read state.json, branch per the decision table above (0-5)\n```\n\n## Phase 0 invariants (selection — full procedure: `references/phase-build.md`)\n\nTest-pinned invariants the build gate's Phase 0 references; they live here so every session carries them.\n\n`autopilot enter` is the first Bash call of a build session: it runs this whole step chain and prints one JSON line (`references/phase-build.md` § \"Enter in one call\").\n\n**Lifecycle directories first.** Before the abort handlers and before PRD selection, as its own Bash call:\n\n```bash\nmkdir -p docs/dev/project-management/prds/backlog docs/dev/project-management/prds/wip docs/dev/project-management/prds/done docs/dev/project-management/prds/hold docs/dev/project-management/reviews docs/dev/tmp docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/reports docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/deferred\n```\n\nIdempotent, safe on every invocation. `mkdir` before any move is mandatory: a move into a missing destination silently misplaces the PRD (`references/design-rationale.md` § Verified moves).\n\nThen, right after that `mkdir -p` and as its own Bash call, run `autopilot ensure-store`: `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/cli/__main__.py ensure-store --state <state.json>`. It writes `docs/dev/project-management/.gitignore`, the machine form of the § Retention Disposable list, whenever that file is missing or differs from the list; it is idempotent, exits 0 either way, and needs no `state.json` to exist yet. Every in-progress resume preserves both fields, including transitions\nto another PRD in the same batch; only a new batch tries a rejected Carl again.\n\n## Phase 3 invariants (work — full procedure: `references/phase-build.md`)\n\n**`work_start_sha` is captured once per PRD.** Run `git rev-parse HEAD` and write it to `state.work_start_sha` before dispatching `/autopilot:work`, but only if it is unset for the current PRD (`state.work_start_sha` absent or empty). Never glob `reports/*.md` to choose a file, and never append to a report whose id differs from `state.batch.id` — a mismatch is a batch-identity error; create a fresh `{state.batch.id}-report.md` instead.\n\n## Design-gate invariant: empty-review-log gate (Phase 1.5 — full procedure: `references/phase-build.md`)\n\nPhase 1.5 must verify the design doc's `## Review log` actually holds at least one reviewer dispatch summary line — a silently-skipped review leaves it empty, and nothing else checks that the review ran. Run the gate on this success path (after a successful `/autopilot:design-solution` run) AND on this artifact-reuse path (when an existing design doc is reused); `design_mode == \"skip\"` bypasses the empty-review-log gate entirely (no doc exists by design). Inline the design-doc path from `state.design_doc` directly into this exact section-scoped check (one `awk`, no pipe, no shell variable — assignments break permission-prefix matching; exit-code based — it counts only pinned dispatch-summary lines that appear inside the `## Review log` section, so the design doc's own example lines in `## Interfaces & contracts` cannot false-pass it):\n\n```\nawk '/^## Review log/{f=1;next} /^## /{f=0} f && /dispatch [0-9]+ \\((claude|codex|claude-fallback)\\): cardinal-sin [0-9]+, blocker [0-9]+, non-blocker [0-9]+, question [0-9]+/{hit=1} END{exit !hit}' <path-from-state.design_doc>\n```\n\n- **exit 0** (≥1 in-section dispatch summary line) → proceed to Phase 2 (planning).\n- **exit non-zero** (empty `## Review log` — the review never ran) → treat as a sub-skill failure: set `state.phase = \"paused\"` and `state.next_phase = \"paused\"`, write `state.pause_reason = {\"site\": \"sub_skill_fail\", \"detail\": \"design doc has empty ## Review log (review never ran)\"}`, and do NOT proceed to planning. Surface the remedy: delete the design doc and let Phase 1.5 regenerate it.\n\nThe check is deterministic (the pinned `awk` above), NOT a model judgment.\n\n## Shell Command Rules\n\n- Never call bash `head`, `tail`, `cat`, `grep`, or `find` - a hook blocks them. Use the Read tool (offset/limit), `rg`, or `rg --files` instead. Never pipe between heterogeneous commands and never combine an inspection (read, list, search, diff) with a test, lint or build invocation in one Bash call - run them as separate calls. Pass an explicit `timeout` on every Bash call: 60000 ms for an inspection, 300000 ms for a lint run or a narrow test run, 600000 ms for a full suite or a full build.\n- **Never chain commands** with `&&`, `|`, or `;` in a single Bash call. Use separate Bash tool calls instead.\n- **Never use redirections** like `2>/dev/null`. still failing → `autopilot restore` and retry once more; still failing → write the `state-write-failed` marker (`site: \"statectl_fail\"`) with the raw stderr in `detail`, end the turn, and also report the failure to the user directly — never proceed on the stale state | Retry once; still failing → `autopilot restore` and retry once more; still failing → write the `state-write-failed` marker (`site: \"statectl_fail\"`) with the raw stderr in `detail`, end the turn — the wrapper halts on it and surfaces the detail |\n| Review produces no parseable output | PAUSE, report — don't retry | Re-run the review ONCE; A batch that drained nothing skips it with a line saying so; a QA failure is recorded and swallowed, never turning a successful drain into a failed one. `_AUTOPILOT_AGOGE_CAP` (default 3600s) bounds a hung run.\n\n- **One loop per repo**: a second `autoclaude` on a repo that already has a live loop refuses to start, naming the incumbent loop's PID (both the tracon front-end and the plain/headless path check the loop registry via `scripts/tracon_wrapper_alive.py` before registering). This prevents two loops double-draining the backlog and racing `state.json` writes. Once the wall-clock cap itself is reached, the same idle-silence watchdog applies, or the session is SIGTERMed at twice the cap (the ceiling), whichever comes first.\n\nA PRD whose session metrics ledger spend since `state.prd_budget_since` exceeds `_AUTOPILOT_PRD_BUDGET_USD` (float; default 300; `0` disables; an unparseable value keeps 300) is parked (`park_site: \"budget\"`) rather than left to burn further sessions unattended.\n\nThe agoge run above arms the runtime-security lane by default, passing `--authorized autoclaude-drain`; `_AUTOPILOT_AGOGE_AUTHORIZED=0` is the kill switch, dropping just that flag so QA still runs, unarmed. It brakes a default-on assertion; it is not a separate way to invoke one, since the assertion itself stays invocation-only.\n\n### Task Counts\n\n`tasks_total` and `tasks_completed` are maintained by whoever writes the `state.tasks` snapshot: recompute both in the same write — `tasks_total = len(tasks)`, `tasks_completed = count(status == \"completed\")` (the pidash-era PostToolUse sync hook is retired, PRD 00063). Keep `state.tasks` accurate at phase transitions and recompute the counts alongside each `tasks` snapshot, applying all three with `statectl set` (§ State Management), keeping the dashboard progress bar live.\n\n### Live Dashboard\n\n`autoclaude` launches `tracon` (`scripts/tracon/`) in the foreground by default (PRD 00062), so the loop terminal shows the live dashboard with no extra step. Full operator surface: `references/dashboard-format.md`.\n\n### Phase Banners\n\nPrint a banner at each phase transition:\n\n```\n── AUTOPILOT ── PRD: {prd-name} ── Phase: {PHASE} ──────────────────\n── AUTOPILOT ── PRD: {prd-name} ── Phase: REVIEW ── Cycle {n} ─────\n── AUTOPILOT ── PRD: {prd-name} ── Cycle {n} rework complete ───────\n── AUTOPILOT ── handing off to fresh session for cycle {n+1} ───────\n── AUTOPILOT ── PAUSED ── {n} issue(s) need your decision ──────────\n── AUTOPILOT ── PRD: {prd-name} ── DONE ── {n} cycles ─────────────\n```\n\n## Session Loop\n\nUnattended mode runs each session headless: the `autoclaude` wrapper (in `~/.config/bash/plugins/development.plugin.bash`) hands off to `autopilot loop` — the CLI loop driver, `cli/loop.py` (PRD 00106) — which launches `claude -p \"/autopilot:run-autopilot\"`; the session runs exactly one turn, and the process exits at turn end. There is no signal file and no Stop-hook choreography — **`state.json` is the entire hand-off contract** (`references/design-rationale.md` § Headless sessions). For a single hand-off rather than a whole batch — the hybrid track's fresh-session review and finalize hops — run `autopilot review-once`: it runs the same preflights and one routed session for `state.next_phase`, then exits, never relaunching or parking, and refuses any phase but `review` or `done` before spawning. Export `_AUTOPILOT_WRITE_SCOPE_EXTRA` first when the project spans roots outside its repo (`~/.claude/AGENTS.md` § Toolchain), same as for a batch. Each launch passes `--strict-mcp-config --mcp-config <value>` so a loop session loads only the Context7 MCP server instead of every claude.ai connector on the account; `_AUTOPILOT_MCP_CONFIG=inherit` restores the unscoped launch, and any other value overrides the config verbatim (`mcp_config_for`, `cli/runner.py`).\n\n**Hand-off = write state, print banner, end the turn.** After the process exits, the loop driver reads `state.json` and branches:\n\n0. `state-write-failed` marker present → stop the loop and notify with its `detail`, without needing `state.json` to be readable.\n1. `pause_reason` set or `phase == \"paused\"` → notify the user with the pause detail, stop the loop, state left intact.\n2. `stall_reason.stalled == \"subagent_prompt_overrun\"` (set by `/autopilot:work`'s Subagent Dispatch Budget when an assembled subagent prompt exceeded 50K after one trim pass; `/autopilot:work` also appends to `state.task_aborts`) → continue the loop; Phase 0 of the next session replans the PRD in place (PRD stays in `wip/`; see the build gate's abort handlers). This is the one surviving replan path.\n3. `next_phase == \"\"` (empty) → backlog drained: the loop archives `state.json` to `reports/{batch_id}-state-final.json`, notifies, and stops the loop.\n4. `next_phase` non-empty → relaunch a fresh session, which resumes from state by artifact — capsule fresh → skip catchup, tasks exist → skip planning, `/autopilot:work` continues at the first non-completed task.\n5. `state.json` missing, unreadable, or untouched by the session → first a stand-down check: a `pause-requested` marker written during the session means the session found another session owning its PRD and stood down on purpose (the stand-down procedure below) — the loop consumes the marker, stamps `paused-by-operator`, notifies with the marker's reason, and stops with state intact; no retry burned, no park marker, `autoclaude` alone resumes (PRD 00172). Otherwise a usage-limit check against the captured session log (`last-session.log`; a live limit means sleep-until-reset and continue). Otherwise a genuine death: with a PRD selected (`state.prd` non-empty) the loop retries the relaunch once (`_AUTOPILOT_DIED_RETRIES_MAX`, default 1), then on exhaustion PARKS it — writes `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/park-requested` (`{prd, reason}`) and relaunches, so the next session's Phase 0 park handler sidelines the sick PRD to `hold/` and the batch keeps draining (PRD 00066). Only a **bootstrap** death (no PRD selected — nothing to park) notifies \"died\" and stops loud; an unconsumed park marker trips the loop's park-loop guard (also a loud stop; guarded relaunches back off `_AUTOPILOT_PARK_BACKOFF`, default 30s, and a marker whose write fails outright halts loud rather than handing off an empty marker). These two are rows 8 and 10 of the Error Handling § sanctioned batch-halt list.\n\nA Work-turn context-cap overrun is just branch 4: `autopilot_context_cap_hook.py` records the rotation (appends to `state.cap_rotations`, resets the in-flight task to `pending`, sets `next_phase: \"build\"`), the turn ends, and the fresh session resumes `build` by artifact — NO replan.\n\n**Stand-down procedure (a peer session owns the PRD).** A headless session never works a PRD another session is already working: two writers on one `state.json` and one set of task artifacts corrupt both, and the one-loop-per-repo guard sees only wrappers, not a bare interactive session. Phase 0 asks before it pauses. A peer counts only when `ListAgents` shows a busy interactive session whose name starts with this repository's directory basename (`basename \"$PWD\"`, e.g. `agent-skills-`); a session named for another repository is never evidence, whatever it is busy with (the two 2026-09-14 false stand-downs in agent-skills each cited a `claude-autopilot-*` session, the other repo's own loop). When such a peer exists, send it one `SendMessage` naming the PRD and wait at most 120 s for a reply. Stand down only when the reply claims the PRD (condition `peer_claimed`), or when writer evidence is present: `autopilot dirty` prints at least one path (condition `dirty_tree`; store writes never count as this evidence), or the mtime of `state.json` or `contract-card.md`, truncated to whole seconds, is greater than the `at` of the most recent `kind: \"handoff\"` row with `edge: \"leave\"` and this PRD's `prd` in `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/dispatch-metrics.jsonl` (condition `state_after_leave`; the rows carry no batch id, so the `prd` filter is what keeps an older batch's row out; when no such `leave` row exists, skip the mtime test and let the dirty-tree test and the reply decide). That comparison holds only because every handoff site writes its `leave` row AFTER its last state and card write (§ Session handoff procedure orders step 1 before step 2; `/autopilot:work`'s task-boundary handoff must set `next_phase` before its row too): a site that touches `state.json` after its row makes every next session read its own hand-off as peer evidence. A bare recent mtime is not evidence (a reader that inspects state while the loop writes, or this batch's own per-PRD reset, satisfies it), commit trailers are not consulted (no commit here carries a session trailer), and a peer that only reads, or never answers, never pauses a batch. To stand down: do not select, move, or write anything else; write `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/pause-requested` with the Write tool as one JSON line, `{\"reason\": \"<peer session> owns <prd> (<evidence>)\", \"condition\": \"<peer_claimed | dirty_tree | state_after_leave>\"}`, and end the turn. The loop reads a marker written during the session as a stand-down (branch 5 above): it stops with state intact, burns no retry, writes no park marker, quotes the reason in its stop line and notification, and records `stood_down` and `stood_down_condition` in the session's `loop-metrics.jsonl` row; `autoclaude` alone resumes once the peer is done. Before this procedure existed (2026-09-02, agent-skills PRD 00010) four stand-downs read as deaths and parked a healthy PRD mid-task.\n\nThe model's only job at a hand-off is to write `state.next_phase` (and `phase`/`stall_reason`) accurately, print the banner, and end the turn. The model never writes any signal and never inspects the loop's decision table — writing accurate state IS the hand-off. Interactive (non-loop) semantics are identical minus the loop: the same state writes happen, and the user re-invokes `/autopilot:run-autopilot` manually.\n\n**End the turn only at a real hand-off.** A phase is complete only when its artifacts are written and `state` is advanced (`phases_completed` updated, `next_phase` set). Dispatched work — `Agent` calls and background Bash — returns its results **within the same headless turn**: the harness re-invokes you with each `<task-notification>` before the turn can end, so dispatch, overlap independent work, wait for the results, and finish the phase. Do not end the turn to \"wait for\" something you dispatched.\n\n**Background Bash alone cannot hold a headless session open.** Documented `-p` behavior: live subagents keep the process alive across turn ends and re-invoke on completion, but background Bash tasks are killed ~5s after the final result. A turn that ends while ONLY background Bash (codex/gemini/qwen, `cargo test`, …) is still running kills that work and strands the phase (2026-07-12: the review session died this way twice — codex killed mid-review, state untouched, loop halted). Whenever dispatched background Bash may outlive every live subagent, dispatch a **Watcher subagent** in the same message that re-runs `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/review-work-completion/scripts/await_reviewer_outputs.py` against the expected output files until `DONE` (procedure: `/autopilot:review-work-completion` step 5). If genuine work cannot finish in this session, that is a PAUSE (`phase: \"paused\"` + `state.pause_reason = {\"site\": \"work_incomplete\", \"detail\": \"<what could not finish>\"}` + end turn), not a silent idle stop.\n\n### Session handoff procedure (canonical — gate files invoke it by site name)\n\nEvery session handoff is the same three steps:\n\n1. **Apply the transition** with one `autopilot phase-done --outcome <outcome>` call (table below). It reads the current phase from `state.json`, looks the pair up in `cli/transitions.py`, and commits the next phase together with every field effect that transition mandates — in ONE transaction. To survive that, **at each gate transition write a compact contract card** — the current step, the active invariants, and the next gate:\n\n- **Autopilot (state.json world):** write the body to `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/contract-card.md` with the **Write tool**, then load it with one call:\n  ```bash\n  python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/scripts/statectl.py <state.json> set-contract-card docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/contract-card.md\n  ```\n  Keep it a few lines: `step: <phase/step> | invariants: <the 2-3 that bind right now> | next: <the next gate + its precondition>`. **Never pass the card as an inline shell argument** — it carries quotes, newlines and `$`, and the inline `set contract_card '<string>'` form failed three consecutive times on quoting in a real build session (2026-08-02, engram session 6).\n- **Interactive (no state.json):** the file write above is the whole step; skip the statectl call.\n\nThe session brief (`write-brief`, § Session handoff procedure step 2) is rendered right after this call so it carries the card just loaded; `/autopilot:work`'s task-boundary handoff and `/autopilot:review-work-completion`'s cycle transition write the brief the same way where they write their cards.\n\n`reinject_contract_card.py` is a SessionStart hook **matched to `compact` only** (startup/resume/clear stay unmatched, so there is no standing token cost); after a compaction it reads the card back and re-injects it as additionalContext. `/autopilot:work` (task-boundary transitions) and `/autopilot:review-work-completion` (cycle transitions) write their own cards the same way — `contract_card` in `references/state-schema.md`.\n\n### Loop Detection\n\nThe `autoclaude` wrapper exports `_AUTOPILOT_LOOP=$$` before launching each headless session. Skills branch on it for loop-mode behavior only — the `AskUserQuestion` ban (Error Handling), git-push deferral, notify suppression in `~/.claude/hooks/notify.py`. Exit-2 Stop-hook blocking works in `-p` mode (`references/design-rationale.md` § Review-file gate). This is a completeness gate on review artifacts, not loop orchestration.\n\n**State-write gate (in-session integrity gate).** `statectl` is the normal writer and cannot produce an invalid `state.json`, but a stray hand-edit still can, so `validate_state_json_hook.py` stays registered on PostToolUse for the `Edit`/`Write`/`MultiEdit` matchers: any such mutation that leaves the file unparseable exit-2-feeds the parse error back to the model immediately, while the session can still rewrite it. Without it, the corruption surfaces only at session exit, where the wrapper's `jq` check misreads a healthy PAUSE as `died` (state file unreadable) and halts the loop (harness-tag bleed appended `</content>` to a hand-edited write, ddb 2026-07-16).\n\n**Loop sketch** (the real driver — `cli/loop.py`, invoked as `autopilot loop` — adds the memory circuit-breaker, the session wall-clock cap, orphan cleanup, metrics, notifications, and the operator-view renderer — `scripts/render_stream.py` turns the stream-json terminal output into one-line summaries while `last-session.log` keeps the raw events; the bash `autoclaude` wrapper keeps only the operator subcommands, the tracon presentation front-end, and the hand-off):\n\n```\nautoclaude                 # bash: subcommands + tracon front-end, then\n  -> autopilot loop        # cli/loop.py, the driver:\n       while True:\n           pause marker?  -> consume it, notify, stop\n           spawn the routed `claude -p \"/autopilot:run-autopilot\"` (raw events kept in last-session.log)\n           read state.json, branch per the decision table above (0-5)\n```\n\n## Phase 0 invariants (selection — full procedure: `references/phase-build.md`)\n\nTest-pinned invariants the build gate's Phase 0 references; they live here so every session carries them.\n\n`autopilot enter` is the first Bash call of a build session: it runs this whole step chain and prints one JSON line (`references/phase-build.md` § \"Enter in one call\").\n\n**Lifecycle directories first.** Before the abort handlers and before PRD selection, as its own Bash call:\n\n```bash\nmkdir -p docs/dev/project-management/prds/backlog docs/dev/project-management/prds/wip docs/dev/project-management/prds/done docs/dev/project-management/prds/hold docs/dev/project-management/reviews docs/dev/tmp docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/reports docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/deferred\n```\n\nIdempotent, safe on every invocation. `mkdir` before any move is mandatory: a move into a missing destination silently misplaces the PRD (`references/design-rationale.md` § Verified moves).\n\nThen, right after that `mkdir -p` and as its own Bash call, run `autopilot ensure-store`: `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/cli/__main__.py ensure-store --state <state.json>`. It writes `docs/dev/project-management/.gitignore`, the machine form of the § Retention Disposable list, whenever that file is missing or differs from the list; it is idempotent, exits 0 either way, and needs no `state.json` to exist yet. The file is written by code, never with the Write or Edit tool: `hooks/enforce_prd_location.py` rejects a top-level store file outside its keeper list for editor tools, and that refusal is correct and stays. This avoids pulling in optional/heavy dependencies before the user picks a subcommand:\n\n```python\n@cli.command(\"create\")\n@click.pass_context\ndef create(ctx):\n    from bim.commands.create_note.create_note import CommandCreateNote\n    ...\n```\n\n## Error Handling\n\n**Command layer** (`commands/`):\n- Return `CommandResult` for all outcomes — success and failure\n- Catch expected exceptions (e.g. `FileNotFoundError`) internally, return `CommandResult(success=False, error=str(exc))`\n- No `console.panic()` or `sys.exit()` inside command classes\n- No custom exception classes for control flow\n\n**CLI layer** (`cli.py`):\n- Inspect `CommandResult` and call `console.panic()` / `console.failure()` / `console.success()`\n- Use `console.report_result()` for standardized output\n- Catch `ImportError` for optional deps, call `console.require_import()`\n- Catch `FatalError` for unrecoverable infrastructure failures\n\n**Click argument validation**:\n- Avoid parse-time validators that short-circuit before the callback (`click.Path(exists=True)`, `IntRange`, custom `ParamType.convert` that raises). They emit Click's default `Usage: ... Error: ...` formatting and bypass the buvis console.\n- Validate inside the callback instead: `if not path.is_file(): console.panic(f\"file not found: {path}\"); return`.\n- `click.Choice` is the exception — its parse-time error lists the valid values, which is more useful than a rewritten message.\n\n**Console methods**:\n- Fatal (exit): `console.panic(msg)` — prints + exits with code 1\n- Recoverable: `console.failure(msg)` — prints, continues\n- Status: `console.success()`, `console.warning()`, `console.info()`\n- All user-facing output must route through `console`. No `print()`, `sys.stdout.write()`, `sys.stderr.write()`, `click.echo()`, `click.secho()`, or the Python logging module. Plain writes bypass the buvis prefix markers (`✘`, `✓`, etc.) and become indistinguishable from stray output, which is what makes a missed `console.panic` look like a print statement to the user.\n- The one sanctioned exception is the `dot filter` clean/smudge plumbing, which writes git's blob payload as raw bytes on stdout and at most one error line on stderr, because git owns both streams and a console marker would corrupt the payload (discovery R12).\n- Never let raw exceptions (stack traces) reach the user.\n\n## Invariants (evolution guardrails)\n\nThese encode the failure classes surfaced by the 2026-07-09 evolution assessment (`docs/dev/project-management/reviews/evolution-assessment-2026-07-09.md`). Each is either **HOLDS** (enforce it) or a **GAP** (a tracked PRD is closing it — write new code to the target state, not the current one).\n\n- **Atomic persistence** — never persist a note, state file, or config with a bare `Path.write_text`/`open(...,\"w\")`. Use `pybase.filesystem.atomic_write` (tempfile + fsync + `os.replace`). Truncate-then-write loses data on crash/ENOSPC. *HOLDS for the library and note/updater write paths (00041) — keep it, except `ConfigWriter.write` (`configuration/config_writer.py`), which still does a bare `write_text` — deliberately out of scope for 00041. GAP → pidash was closed by retiring pidash (00071); autopilot-state durability now lives in the buvis home repo (tracon/statectl), not gems.*\n- **Confine request-derived paths** — any filesystem path built from an HTTP request / external input must be `resolve()`d and asserted under an allowed root before read/write/delete/open. Network-facing servers must have auth + `TrustedHostMiddleware`. *HOLDS (00042) — bim serve confines request paths via `confine_path` (403 outside the vault/archive roots), mints a startup token required as `X-Buvis-Token`, installs `TrustedHostMiddleware`, and warns on a non-loopback bind (`commands/serve/_security.py`). Keep it.*\n- **The library stays interface-agnostic** — `src/lib/buvis/pybase/` must not import a UI framework at module import time or emit output outside the console adapter. No import-time Click monkey-patching, no `sys.exit`/`click.echo`/`print` in lib code. A TUI/API/WebUI process must be able to `import` settings without pulling Click. *HOLDS (00052) — keep it.*\n- **One action, one implementation across interfaces** — CLI/TUI/API/WebUI adapters must drive the same command class / use case through the composition root and return `CommandResult`; do not reimplement business logic per interface (dot's TUI is the anti-pattern; bim's serve action registry is the exemplar). *HOLDS (00051 design → 00053/00054) — the all-interface seam design (00051) is realized: dot's git ops unified behind `DotGitService` (00053) and bim's serve/TUI converged on the shared action registry (00054). Keep it.*\n- **Claim/lifecycle release on any exit** — resource claims and locks release in `finally` (or catch `BaseException`), never only `except Exception`; `KeyboardInterrupt` must not leak a claim. *HOLDS (00044) — the bim doc claim/dedup pipeline releases claims and locks in `finally` (`commands/doc/shared/`); keep it.*\n- **`CommandResult` discipline** — commands return `CommandResult`; the CLI/adapter layer renders it (`console.report_result`) and maps exit/HTTP status. No `sys.exit`/`console.panic` inside command classes. *HOLDS in `src/tools/*/commands/**` — keep it.*\n- **Clean-architecture layering + tool isolation** — zettel `domain → application → infrastructure → integrations` one-directional; no cross-tool imports; no `src/lib → src/tools`. *HOLDS — keep it.*\n\n## Testing\n\n- pytest + pytest-mock + pytest-cov\n- Tests in `tests/` mirror `src/lib/` and `src/tools/` structure\n- Mock subprocess calls heavily\n- Class-based test organization\n- **No unused imports/variables**\n- **Markers**: `pytest -m <tool>` runs one tool, `pytest -m lib` runs library tests, `pytest -m \"not bim\"` excludes a tool. Auto-applied by path in `tests/conftest.py` — no decorators needed. Scaffold registers markers for new tools.\n- **Snapshot tests** (`@pytest.mark.snapshot`) only run on the canonical env (Linux + Python 3.12) — SVG output from Rich/Textual differs across OS/Python so baselines must come from one place. Force locally with `BUVIS_SNAPSHOT_CANONICAL=1` only if you know what you're doing.\n\n## Installation\n\n```bash\nuv tool install buvis-gems              # core only (no tool-specific deps)\nuv tool install buvis-gems[bim]         # with jira support\nuv tool install buvis-gems[bim-web]     # bim web UI deps\nuv tool install buvis-gems[all]         # everything\nuv tool upgrade buvis-gems              # update\n```\n\nExtras: `bim`, `bim-web`, `doc`, `dot`, `fren`, `morph`, `muc`, `pinger`, `postup`, `postup-web`, `readerctl`, `all`\n\n## Release\n\n> Full procedure (version authority, checks, destinations, partial-failure recovery): `docs/dev/procedures/releasing.md`.\n\n```bash\nrelease patch|minor|major              # bump, tag, push → CI publishes to PyPI\nrelease --pre rc1                      # pre-release current version to TestPyPI\nrelease --pre rc1 minor                # bump + pre-release to TestPyPI\nrelease                                # after rc: strip suffix, release stable to PyPI\nrelease local                          # build .devN wheel + install locally\nrelease --dry-run [--pre rc1] [patch]  # preview without changes\n```\n\n`mise` adds `tools` to PATH (shims; `tools/lib` holds the implementations). Tags with `rc` in the name publish to TestPyPI; stable tags go to PyPI. Manual workflow dispatch defaults to TestPyPI.\n\n**First-time setup** (already done for buvis-gems):\n- test.pypi.org: add trusted publisher (owner: `buvis`, repo: `gems`, workflow: `publish.yml`, env: `testpypi`)\n- GitHub repo settings: create `testpypi` and `pypi` environments\n\n**Why explicit version in pyproject.toml?** maturin reads the version from `pyproject.toml` at build time to compile the Rust extension. Tag-based versioning (hatch-vcs) would require glue to inject the version before maturin sees it. Other provider hosts use their host mapping.\n\n# Autopilot\n\nOrchestrate the full PRD lifecycle: catchup → design → plan-tasks → work → review-rework loop (consensus + blind + doubt lenses, every cycle) → done.\n\nMakes autonomous decisions backed by research (dependencies, recurring issues, API/schema changes when PRD-driven) and pauses only for critical security, requirements ambiguity, or blocking decisions.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- Pack skills (invoked as phases): `design-solution`, `plan-tasks`, `work`,\n  `review-work-completion`\n- Plugin skills: `git-ferry:catchup` (Phase 1, unless the PRD sets `catchup: skip`)\n- Files read from other skill dirs:\n  `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/review-work-completion/scripts/await_reviewer_outputs.py`\n  (Watcher keep-alive)\n- Hooks outside the skill dir: `~/.claude/hooks/notify.py`\n- Shell wrapper outside `~/.claude`: `autoclaude` in\n  `~/.config/bash/plugins/development.plugin.bash` - operator subcommands +\n  tracon front-end; it hands off to `autopilot loop` (`cli/loop.py`), the\n  unattended session loop since PRD 00106\n- Scripts (own dir, model-invoked as a CLI): `scripts/statectl.py` — the sole\n  `state.json` mutator (`get`/`set`/`append`/`del`; atomic, advisory-locked,\n  one rotating `.bak`)\n- CLIs: `claude` (headless `-p`), `python3` (>= 3.11), `git`, `awk`\n- Optional: `tracon` (`scripts/tracon/`; the default `autoclaude` front-end since PRD 00062, `_AUTOPILOT_TRACON=0` or no tty/`uv` falls back to `render_stream.py`) - dashboard only, absence changes nothing\n\n## Execution Model\n\n**Run all phases in sequence without stopping.** After each phase completes, immediately update state and proceed to the next phase. Do not pause between phases, do not summarize progress, do not wait for user input - unless the phase explicitly says PAUSE or STOP. Completing a sub-skill invocation (`/git-ferry:catchup`, `/autopilot:plan-tasks`, `/autopilot:work`, `/autopilot:review-work-completion`, etc.) is NOT a stopping point. It is an intermediate step. Continue.\n\nReview sessions run on opus at xhigh in cycle 1 and at high on cycle 2 and later; _AUTOPILOT_EFFORT_REVIEW forces one effort for every cycle and _AUTOPILOT_EFFORT_REVIEW_RERUN sets the rerun value. A rework resume (the cycle's review file exists and `rework_task_ids` names an unfinished task) runs on the queued tasks' own tier instead, sonnet unless one is opus or fable (`references/model-ladder.md` § Review sessions, PRD 00207).\n\n## Entry Points\n\n- `/autopilot:run-autopilot` — auto-select PRD (wip first, then backlog), run full cycle\n- `/autopilot:run-autopilot <prd-filename>` — full cycle with specific PRD\n- `/autopilot:run-autopilot status` — print current dashboard, no action\n- `/autopilot:run-autopilot review-batch` — interactively review a finished batch's deferred items\n\nIf invoked with `status`, read `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json`, print phase/cycle/task summary, and stop.\n\nIf invoked with `review-batch`, load the newest `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/deferred/{batch_id}-deferred.json` and run the \"Batch-End Review\" presentation (`references/phase-done.md`) against it — chunked by PRD, wait for user decisions, execute \"fix now\" items. This keeps a completed PRD's complete review trail intact after the batch closes (`references/design-rationale.md` § Verified moves).\n\n### Resuming\n\nWhen `/autopilot:run-autopilot` is invoked and `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json` exists with `batch.completed_prds`, this is a continuation after a session restart. Preserve `batch.completed_prds` (including `batch.id`) and proceed to the build gate's Phase 0 to pick the next PRD.\n\nDelete `state.pause_reason` from `state.json` if present — unconditional, on every invocation, NOT gated on `batch.completed_prds`. A new session means any pause is being resumed; `pause_reason` belongs only to an unresolved pause and is not overwritten by normal progression, so it must be cleared here or it halts the resumed PRD's next hand-off. Cap-pause detection is unaffected — it keys on `cap_pause_reason`, which this delete does not touch.\n\n### Operator runbook (unattended batches)\n\nAll interaction with a running `autoclaude` batch happens at session boundaries — the only safe point. (Operator-shell commands for the human's own terminal, not for the model's Bash tool — `tail -f` would hang a session and pipes are hook-blocked.)\n\n- **Watch**: `tail -f docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/last-session.log` — the wrapper tees the live event log of the running headless turn there.\n- **Pause**: `touch docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/pause-requested` — the wrapper consumes the marker at the next session boundary, notifies \"paused by operator\", and stops the loop with state intact. It leaves `paused-by-operator` behind so tracon shows `⏸ paused` rather than `⚠ orphaned`; plain `autoclaude` resumes (nothing to clear, no decision to make). The marker may carry a JSON reason, `{\"reason\": \"...\"}`, which the stop line and the notification quote; a session that stands down for a peer writes one with a `condition` beside it, after asking the peer first (§ Session Loop, stand-down procedure).\n- **Take over**: with the loop stopped (pause marker, or Ctrl-C on the wrapper), run `/autopilot:run-autopilot` in a normal interactive session — resume-by-artifact reads the same `state.json`, and full interactive semantics (questions, PAUSEs) apply because `$_AUTOPILOT_LOOP` is unset. Restart `autoclaude` afterwards to go unattended again.\n- **Resume after a PAUSE** (`phase: \"paused\"` in `state.json`, \"session paused\" banner/ntfy): same take-over recipe, and it is the ONLY way forward — re-running `autoclaude` reads the paused state and exits again immediately. Interactively, the phase that paused re-runs with `AskUserQuestion` available, so the blockers that halted the loop are asked as decisions instead. Answer them, let the session hand off or finish the PRD, then re-run `autoclaude`.\n- **Un-park a sidelined PRD**: a PRD the loop parked (a `wrapper_died` death-park, or a loop-mode `design_gate` / `blocking_escalation` stall) sits in `docs/dev/project-management/prds/hold/` with its stall recorded in the batch deferred JSON; the batch kept draining without it. To resume it, `mv docs/dev/project-management/prds/hold/<00XXX-…>.md docs/dev/project-management/prds/backlog/` (keep the `00XXX-` prefix). Autopilot never reads `hold/`, so the next `/autopilot:run-autopilot` (or `autoclaude` relaunch) re-selects it from `backlog/` and re-enters the build gate, reusing its existing design doc via the Phase 1.5 artifact skip (a `design_gate` park then re-fires the gate interactively). Batch-end review lists every parked PRD (`{m} stalled`), so none is silently forgotten.\n- **Forensics**: `claude --resume <session-id>` (the id is in the init event at the top of `last-session.log`) reopens a finished headless conversation for questioning. Full operator surface, including what is deferred: `references/waves.md`.\n- **Product QA (agoge)**: once a batch drains at least one PRD, the loop runs a single product-QA pass (`/run-agoge` over the repo), logging to `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/reports/{batch}-agoge.log`. A batch that drained nothing skips it with a line saying so; a QA failure is recorded and swallowed, never turning a successful drain into a failed one. `_AUTOPILOT_AGOGE_CAP` (default 3600s) bounds a hung run.\n\n- **One loop per repo**: a second `autoclaude` on a repo that already has a live loop refuses to start, naming the incumbent loop's PID (both the tracon front-end and the plain/headless path check the loop registry via `scripts/tracon_wrapper_alive.py` before registering). This prevents two loops double-draining the backlog and racing `state.json` writes. If the refusal is wrong (the named PID is dead), the stale registry entry is pruned automatically on the next launch; force it by deleting `~/.claude/autopilot-loops/<pid>.json`.\n\nA running headless turn is interrupted by the wrapper's wall-clock cap (`_AUTOPILOT_SESSION_MAX`, default 7200s; review-phase launches use `_AUTOPILOT_SESSION_MAX_REVIEW`, default 10800s) and, independently, by the idle watchdog at any point after launch: it kills a session whose log has gone silent for `_AUTOPILOT_SESSION_IDLE` seconds (default 1200s; `0` disables pre-cap idle kill, restoring the old kill-at-cap-only behavior) as long as nothing is in flight (`session_busy`) - this fires before the cap, not only past it.
