Once the wall-clock cap itself is reached, the same idle-silence watchdog applies, or the session is SIGTERMed at twice the cap (the ceiling), whichever comes first.\n\nA PRD whose session metrics ledger spend since `state.prd_budget_since` exceeds `_AUTOPILOT_PRD_BUDGET_USD` (float; default 300; `0` disables; an unparseable value keeps 300) is parked (`park_site: \"budget\"`) rather than left to burn further sessions unattended.\n\nThe agoge run above arms the runtime-security lane by default, passing `--authorized autoclaude-drain`; `_AUTOPILOT_AGOGE_AUTHORIZED=0` is the kill switch, dropping just that flag so QA still runs, unarmed. Only the literal `0` disables it: anything else, including `false`, `no`, `off`, or `0` with a trailing space, leaves it armed, because a security brake should fail toward armed, not away from it. It brakes a default-on assertion; it is not a separate way to invoke one, since the assertion itself stays invocation-only.\n\n### Task Counts\n\n`tasks_total` and `tasks_completed` are maintained by whoever writes the `state.tasks` snapshot: recompute both in the same write — `tasks_total = len(tasks)`, `tasks_completed = count(status == \"completed\")` (the pidash-era PostToolUse sync hook is retired, PRD 00063). The model does not re-derive these counts by any other means; the arithmetic runs on the snapshot already in hand. Keep `state.tasks` accurate at phase transitions and recompute the counts alongside each `tasks` snapshot, applying all three with `statectl set` (§ State Management), keeping the dashboard progress bar live.\n\n### Live Dashboard\n\n`autoclaude` launches `tracon` (`scripts/tracon/`) in the foreground by default (PRD 00062), so the loop terminal shows the live dashboard with no extra step. It reads `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json` — no action needed from autopilot beyond keeping the state file updated. `q` detaches (loop keeps running, wrapper prints the reattach command), `p` pauses at the next session boundary, `Ctrl-C` stops the loop with full cleanup. When there is no tty, no `uv`, or `_AUTOPILOT_TRACON=0`, the loop terminal shows the `render_stream.py` fallback with per-lane subagent tags instead. Full operator surface: `references/dashboard-format.md`.\n\n### Phase Banners\n\nPrint a banner at each phase transition:\n\n```\n── AUTOPILOT ── PRD: {prd-name} ── Phase: {PHASE} ──────────────────\n── AUTOPILOT ── PRD: {prd-name} ── Phase: REVIEW ── Cycle {n} ─────\n── AUTOPILOT ── PRD: {prd-name} ── Cycle {n} rework complete ───────\n── AUTOPILOT ── handing off to fresh session for cycle {n+1} ───────\n── AUTOPILOT ── PAUSED ── {n} issue(s) need your decision ──────────\n── AUTOPILOT ── PRD: {prd-name} ── DONE ── {n} cycles ─────────────\n```\n\n## Session Loop\n\nUnattended mode runs each session headless: the `autoclaude` wrapper (in `~/.config/bash/plugins/development.plugin.bash`) hands off to `autopilot loop` — the CLI loop driver, `cli/loop.py` (PRD 00106) — which launches `claude -p \"/autopilot:run-autopilot\"`; the session runs exactly one turn, and the process exits at turn end. There is no signal file and no Stop-hook choreography — **`state.json` is the entire hand-off contract** (`references/design-rationale.md` § Headless sessions). For a single hand-off rather than a whole batch — the hybrid track's fresh-session review and finalize hops — run `autopilot review-once`: it runs the same preflights and one routed session for `state.next_phase`, then exits, never relaunching or parking, and refuses any phase but `review` or `done` before spawning. Export `_AUTOPILOT_WRITE_SCOPE_EXTRA` first when the project spans roots outside its repo (`~/.claude/AGENTS.md` § Toolchain), same as for a batch. Each launch passes `--strict-mcp-config --mcp-config <value>` so a loop session loads only the Context7 MCP server instead of every claude.ai connector on the account; `_AUTOPILOT_MCP_CONFIG=inherit` restores the unscoped launch, and any other value overrides the config verbatim (`mcp_config_for`, `cli/runner.py`).\n\n**Hand-off = write state, print banner, end the turn.** After the process exits, the loop driver reads `state.json` and branches:\n\n0. `state-write-failed` marker present → stop the loop and notify with its `detail`, without needing `state.json` to be readable.\n1. `pause_reason` set or `phase == \"paused\"` → notify the user with the pause detail, stop the loop, state left intact.\n2. `stall_reason.stalled == \"subagent_prompt_overrun\"` (set by `/autopilot:work`'s Subagent Dispatch Budget when an assembled subagent prompt exceeded 50K after one trim pass; `/autopilot:work` also appends to `state.task_aborts`) → continue the loop; Phase 0 of the next session replans the PRD in place (PRD stays in `wip/`; see the build gate's abort handlers). This is the one surviving replan path.\n3. `next_phase == \"\"` (empty) → backlog drained: the loop archives `state.json` to `reports/{batch_id}-state-final.json`, notifies, and stops the loop.\n4. `next_phase` non-empty → relaunch a fresh session, which resumes from state by artifact — capsule fresh → skip catchup, tasks exist → skip planning, `/autopilot:work` continues at the first non-completed task.\n5. `state.json` missing, unreadable, or untouched by the session → first a stand-down check: a `pause-requested` marker written during the session means the session found another session owning its PRD and stood down on purpose (the stand-down procedure below) — the loop consumes the marker, stamps `paused-by-operator`, notifies with the marker's reason, and stops with state intact; no retry burned, no park marker, `autoclaude` alone resumes (PRD 00172). Otherwise a usage-limit check against the captured session log (`last-session.log`; a live limit means sleep-until-reset and continue). Otherwise a genuine death: with a PRD selected (`state.prd` non-empty) the loop retries the relaunch once (`_AUTOPILOT_DIED_RETRIES_MAX`, default 1), then on exhaustion PARKS it — writes `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/park-requested` (`{prd, reason}`) and relaunches, so the next session's Phase 0 park handler sidelines the sick PRD to `hold/` and the batch keeps draining (PRD 00066). Only a **bootstrap** death (no PRD selected — nothing to park) notifies \"died\" and stops loud; an unconsumed park marker trips the loop's park-loop guard (also a loud stop; guarded relaunches back off `_AUTOPILOT_PARK_BACKOFF`, default 30s, and a marker whose write fails outright halts loud rather than handing off an empty marker). These two are rows 8 and 10 of the Error Handling § sanctioned batch-halt list.\n\nA Work-turn context-cap overrun is just branch 4: `autopilot_context_cap_hook.py` records the rotation (appends to `state.cap_rotations`, resets the in-flight task to `pending`, sets `next_phase: \"build\"`), the turn ends, and the fresh session resumes `build` by artifact — NO replan.\n\n**Stand-down procedure (a peer session owns the PRD).** A headless session never works a PRD another session is already working: two writers on one `state.json` and one set of task artifacts corrupt both, and the one-loop-per-repo guard sees only wrappers, not a bare interactive session. Phase 0 asks before it pauses. A peer counts only when `ListAgents` shows a busy interactive session whose name starts with this repository's directory basename (`basename \"$PWD\"`, e.g. `agent-skills-`); a session named for another repository is never evidence, whatever it is busy with (the two 2026-09-14 false stand-downs in agent-skills each cited a `claude-autopilot-*` session, the other repo's own loop). When such a peer exists, send it one `SendMessage` naming the PRD and wait at most 120 s for a reply. Stand down only when the reply claims the PRD (condition `peer_claimed`), or when writer evidence is present: `autopilot dirty` prints at least one path (condition `dirty_tree`; store writes never count as this evidence), or the mtime of `state.json` or `contract-card.md`, truncated to whole seconds, is greater than the `at` of the most recent `kind: \"handoff\"` row with `edge: \"leave\"` and this PRD's `prd` in `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/dispatch-metrics.jsonl` (condition `state_after_leave`; the rows carry no batch id, so the `prd` filter is what keeps an older batch's row out; when no such `leave` row exists, skip the mtime test and let the dirty-tree test and the reply decide). That comparison holds only because every handoff site writes its `leave` row AFTER its last state and card write (§ Session handoff procedure orders step 1 before step 2; `/autopilot:work`'s task-boundary handoff must set `next_phase` before its row too): a site that touches `state.json` after its row makes every next session read its own hand-off as peer evidence. A bare recent mtime is not evidence (a reader that inspects state while the loop writes, or this batch's own per-PRD reset, satisfies it), commit trailers are not consulted (no commit here carries a session trailer), and a peer that only reads, or never answers, never pauses a batch. To stand down: do not select, move, or write anything else; write `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/pause-requested` with the Write tool as one JSON line, `{\"reason\": \"<peer session> owns <prd> (<evidence>)\", \"condition\": \"<peer_claimed | dirty_tree | state_after_leave>\"}`, and end the turn. The loop reads a marker written during the session as a stand-down (branch 5 above): it stops with state intact, burns no retry, writes no park marker, quotes the reason in its stop line and notification, and records `stood_down` and `stood_down_condition` in the session's `loop-metrics.jsonl` row; `autoclaude` alone resumes once the peer is done. Before this procedure existed (2026-09-02, agent-skills PRD 00010) four stand-downs read as deaths and parked a healthy PRD mid-task.\n\nThe model's only job at a hand-off is to write `state.next_phase` (and `phase`/`stall_reason`) accurately, print the banner, and end the turn. The model never writes any signal and never inspects the loop's decision table — writing accurate state IS the hand-off. Interactive (non-loop) semantics are identical minus the loop: the same state writes happen, and the user re-invokes `/autopilot:run-autopilot` manually.\n\n**End the turn only at a real hand-off.** A phase is complete only when its artifacts are written and `state` is advanced (`phases_completed` updated, `next_phase` set). Dispatched work — `Agent` calls and background Bash — returns its results **within the same headless turn**: the harness re-invokes you with each `<task-notification>` before the turn can end, so dispatch, overlap independent work, wait for the results, and finish the phase. Do not end the turn to \"wait for\" something you dispatched.\n\n**Background Bash alone cannot hold a headless session open.** Documented `-p` behavior: live subagents keep the process alive across turn ends and re-invoke on completion, but background Bash tasks are killed ~5s after the final result. A turn that ends while ONLY background Bash (codex/gemini/qwen, `cargo test`, …) is still running kills that work and strands the phase (2026-07-12: the review session died this way twice — codex killed mid-review, state untouched, loop halted). Whenever dispatched background Bash may outlive every live subagent, dispatch a **Watcher subagent** in the same message that re-runs `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/review-work-completion/scripts/await_reviewer_outputs.py` against the expected output files until `DONE` (procedure: `/autopilot:review-work-completion` step 5). The loop's session runner exports `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS=0` so the subagent wait has no 10-minute ceiling; the session wall-clock cap stays the backstop.\n\nAn idle end-of-turn (phase unfinished, nothing pending) no longer thrashes anything — the loop relaunches and the next session resumes the phase by artifact (self-healing) — but it burns a session start, so treat it as waste, not as a mechanism.\n\nFor long **Bash** (builds, tests), still prefer the FOREGROUND with an explicit `timeout` (up to 600000 ms) so the result is in hand directly. If genuine work cannot finish in this session, that is a PAUSE (`phase: \"paused\"` + `state.pause_reason = {\"site\": \"work_incomplete\", \"detail\": \"<what could not finish>\"}` + end turn), not a silent idle stop.\n\n### Session handoff procedure (canonical — gate files invoke it by site name)\n\nEvery session handoff is the same three steps:\n\n1. **Apply the transition** with one `autopilot phase-done --outcome <outcome>` call (table below). It reads the current phase from `state.json`, looks the pair up in `cli/transitions.py`, and commits the next phase together with every field effect that transition mandates — in ONE transaction. There is no `--phase` flag and no per-effect flag: a caller cannot supply a mismatched phase, and cannot forget an effect.\n2. **Write the session brief, then the `leave` handoff row, then record the store, then print the site's banner** (shown at the invoking site in the gate file). The brief comes first, after the contract card (§ Contract card): `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/scripts/statectl.py <state.json> write-brief docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/session-brief.md` renders `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/session-brief.md` from the state step 1 committed (where the batch stands, the card verbatim, the files the next gate needs), so the next session orients from one page (PRD 00201); the loop's launch prompt names it whenever it exists. A failed write is one stderr line, never a phase failure: carry on to the row. The row is `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/scripts/record_dispatch.py handoff --site <build|review|done> --edge leave --phase <state.phase> --prd <state.prd>`, best-effort (`work/references/subagent-dispatch.md` § Dispatch telemetry); `state.phase` already names the next session's phase because step 1 committed it. A new site row in the table below gets its row from this step, not from a per-site sentence. Under `$_AUTOPILOT_LOOP` the row is also the session's point of no return: `hooks/note_session_leave.py` records it, and `hooks/guard_skill_after_leave.py` denies any `autopilot:*` (or `git-ferry:catchup`) `Skill` call this session makes afterwards, so a session that prints its banner and then re-invokes a gate is stopped by the harness, not only by this prose (PRD 00211). After the row, and as the LAST write before STOP, record the store with `autopilot record-store`: `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/cli/__main__.py record-store --state <state.json> --site <build|review|done> --prd <state.prd>`, best-effort like the row (a failure is one stderr line, never a reason to skip the row or the STOP). It runs at every site in the table below and comes after the row, never between the brief and the row: the row itself appends to the tracked `dispatch-metrics.jsonl`, so only a commit that follows it sweeps that append in.\n3. **End the turn.** In loop mode the loop driver reads `state.json` and relaunches per its decision table above; outside the loop the user re-invokes `/autopilot:run-autopilot` and the same resume logic applies. Do NOT continue into the next gate's phases in this session, even if context budget appears sufficient.\n\n| site | `--outcome` | what the transition commits |\n|------|-------------|-----------------------------|\n| **build → review** (`phase-build.md`, after Phase 3) | `tasks_done` | `phase`/`next_phase: \"review\"`. `phases_completed` unchanged — the build gate leaves no membership marker. `state.tasks` is already current — every producer (`task-add`/`task-start`/`task-done`/`task-set-meta`) writes it directly via `statectl`, so there is nothing to query or snapshot at this handoff. |\n| **review → review** (`phase-review.md` Phase 6, after rework when the loop continues) | `rework` | `phase`/`next_phase: \"review\"`, `cycle` incremented, `rework_task_ids` cleared — all in one commit. `state.tasks` untouched. `phases_completed` unchanged — only convergence adds `\"review\"`. |\n| **review → done** (`phase-review.md`, on loop convergence) | `converged` | `phase`/`next_phase: \"done\"`, and `\"review\"` appended to `phases_completed` — the convergence marker the review gate's loop-level skip reads. Not a handoff — nothing relaunches. The `cycle` increment is the one that has already cost a real batch — the Phase 5 cap gate reads it, and losing it once let a loop run past its cap.\n\n### Contract card (compaction re-anchor)\n\nWithin-session compaction can drop this skill's text mid-procedure, after which the session drifts off-contract with nothing to re-anchor it. To survive that, **at each gate transition write a compact contract card** — the current step, the active invariants, and the next gate:\n\n- **Autopilot (state.json world):** write the body to `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/contract-card.md` with the **Write tool**, then load it with one call:\n  ```bash\n  python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/scripts/statectl.py <state.json> set-contract-card docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/contract-card.md\n  ```\n  Keep it a few lines: `step: <phase/step> | invariants: <the 2-3 that bind right now> | next: <the next gate + its precondition>`. **Never pass the card as an inline shell argument** — it carries quotes, newlines and `$`, and the inline `set contract_card '<string>'` form failed three consecutive times on quoting in a real build session (2026-08-02, engram session 6).\n- **Interactive (no state.json):** the file write above is the whole step; skip the statectl call.\n\nThe session brief (`write-brief`, § Session handoff procedure step 2) is rendered right after this call so it carries the card just loaded; `/autopilot:work`'s task-boundary handoff and `/autopilot:review-work-completion`'s cycle transition write the brief the same way where they write their cards.\n\n`reinject_contract_card.py` is a SessionStart hook **matched to `compact` only** (startup/resume/clear stay unmatched, so there is no standing token cost); after a compaction it reads the card back and re-injects it as additionalContext. `/autopilot:work` (task-boundary transitions) and `/autopilot:review-work-completion` (cycle transitions) write their own cards the same way — `contract_card` in `references/state-schema.md`.\n\n### Loop Detection\n\nThe `autoclaude` wrapper exports `_AUTOPILOT_LOOP=$$` before launching each headless session. Skills branch on it for loop-mode behavior only — the `AskUserQuestion` ban (Error Handling), git-push deferral, notify suppression in `~/.claude/hooks/notify.py`. Hand-off sites do NOT check it: the state writes are the same in and out of the loop.\n\n**Review-file gate (in-session quality gate).** `review_coverage_hook.py` stays registered on Stop: at the done hand-off, when the saved review file is missing or fails the `cli/gate.py` shape check (missing reviewer section, verdict, or tests line — PRD 00016, absorbed into the CLI as `autopilot gate` by PRD 00107), it exit-2-blocks the turn's end and feeds the gap back to the model so the review can be finished before the turn ends. Exit-2 Stop-hook blocking works in `-p` mode (`references/design-rationale.md` § Review-file gate). +# Design: bim create scripting contract
+
+PRD: `docs/dev/project-management/prds/wip/00118-bim-create-scripting-contract-v1.md`.
+
+## Architecture fit
+
+Keep the existing boundary: Click, TUI and serve adapters construct `CreateNoteParams` and call `CommandCreateNote`; the command calls interface-agnostic zettel use cases. Identity defaults remain domain fixers. Allocation, reservation and body insertion belong to `CreateZettelUseCase`. Tag validation, inbox handling and result metadata belong to the bim command. Rendering and process exit status belong to the adapters.
+
+The project capsule confirms atomic persistence and shared command implementations. Keep `MarkdownZettelRepository.save` and its `atomic_write_text` unchanged: an exclusive empty reservation precedes its atomic replacement. No new persistence backend, library dependency on bim, or alternate note writer is needed. PRDs 00119 and 00120 own vault templates and links respectively; this design only provides their body-placement and metadata seams.
+
+## Module placement
+
+Edit existing files; no new production modules:
+
+- `src/lib/buvis/pybase/zettel/domain/entities/zettel/fixers/set_default_date.py` and `set_default_id.py`: local date default and offset-faithful id.
+- `src/lib/buvis/pybase/zettel/application/use_cases/create_zettel_use_case.py`: preparation, body insertion, shared attempt accounting, exclusive reservation and cleanup.
+- `src/tools/bim/params/create_note.py`: body, source and dry-run fields.
+- `src/tools/bim/commands/create_note/create_note.py`: formatter dependency, validation, source ingestion, dry run, metadata and trash move.
+- `src/tools/bim/note_write_cli.py`: four flags, body-file/stdin adaptation, JSON output and failed-result exits for five note commands.
+- `src/tools/bim/note_read_cli.py`: failed-result exits for format/sync/show and missing-query-spec exit.
+- `src/tools/bim/tui/create_note.py` and `src/tools/bim/commands/serve/_actions.py`: inject `get_formatter()` into every `CommandCreateNote` construction. Serve forwards `body`, `source` and `dry_run` through the existing params/command boundary; confine request-derived source paths before forwarding.
+- Existing tests named in the PRD, plus existing TUI/serve adapter tests where constructor expectations change.
+- `src/tools/bim/SKILL.md`, `docs/source/tools/bim.rst`, `CHANGELOG.md`: document flags, payload, tag rules, failure exits and local ids. Add a concise scripted-create example to the existing bim section of `README.md`, as required by the capsule's CLI-documentation convention.
+
+## Interfaces & contracts
+
+### Identity fixers
+
+Signatures remain `set_default_date(zettel_data: ZettelData) -> None` and `set_default_id(zettel_data: ZettelData) -> None`.
+
+- When `metadata.get("date") is None`, assign `datetime.now().astimezone().replace(microsecond=0)`. Preserve any existing date.
+- Set `metadata["id"] = int(metadata["date"].strftime("%Y%m%d%H%M%S"))`. Do not convert the date's timezone. A naive datetime keeps its wall-clock digits. A non-datetime raises `ValueError("Invalid date format")`; retain `ValueError("Invalid ID format")` for a failed numeric conversion.
+- `2024-09-13T12:00:00+02:00` yields `20240913120000`; the same instant expressed as `10:00:00Z` yields `20240913100000`.
+- Existing ids remain unchanged: `ZettelConsistencyService._DEFAULTS` delegates to `domain/services/base.py:apply_defaults`, which calls the id fixer only when `metadata.get("id") is None`. `ensure_consistency` has no id/date comparison. Keep that dispatch guard unchanged; mixed old UTC-derived and new local ids require no migration or re-keying. Test that consistency preserves an existing UTC-derived id alongside a non-UTC date.
+
+### CreateZettelUseCase
+
+Public signatures:
+
+```python
+MAX_ID_ATTEMPTS = 5
+
+def prepare(
+    self, template: ZettelTemplate, answers: dict[str, Any], *, body: str | None = None
+) -> tuple[Path, Zettel]: ...
+
+def execute(
+    self, template: ZettelTemplate, answers: dict[str, Any], *, body: str | None = None
+) -> Path: ...
+```
+
+Keep the constructor unchanged. Both methods use one preparation implementation. Use a private `_prepare` helper with the same template/answers/body inputs plus a remaining-attempt count, returning `(path, zettel, remaining_attempts)`; `prepare` supplies five attempts and discards the count, while `execute` retains the count across reservation retries. The counter is invocation-local, never mutable instance state.
+
+Each candidate consumes one attempt before `template.build_data(answers)`. Inject the body into that fresh data, then run `Zettel(data)` and `ZettelFactory.create(zettel)`. Set `path = self.zettelkasten_path / f"{zettel.id}.md"` and `zettel.get_data().file_path = str(path)`. If occupied, sleep exactly one second before rebuilding if attempts remain. Exhaustion raises `FileExistsError(f"Zettel already exists: {path}")`. At most five builds and four sleeps occur across existence checks and reservation losses combined. A reservation loss consumes the candidate already built, not an additional attempt; sleep once before the next rebuild. A fixed-date template gets the same five attempts and fails without special origin detection.
+
+`prepare` does not create directories, reserve files, save, or run hooks. Its existence checks and collision sleeps are permitted in a dry run.
+
+For a nonempty normalized body, normalize `\r\n` to `\n`, remove leading whitespace-only blank lines, and apply `rstrip()` to the whole body. Preserve indentation of its first content line and internal whitespace. Find the first section whose heading exactly equals `getattr(template, "body_section", None)`; if absent, select section zero. Append with one blank line between existing nonempty section content and the supplied body. Preserve all other sections. If the template supplied no sections, initialize `[(f"# {answers.get('title', '')}", body)]` before the fixers. `body=None` or a body that normalizes to empty leaves template content unchanged. No template protocol or YAML loader change is required in this PRD.
+
+For an available candidate, `execute` calls `os.open(path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_WRONLY, 0o600)`, then closes the descriptor. Only a `FileExistsError` from reservation counts as a retryable collision. Call `writer.save(zettel)` once after reservation succeeds. The writer retains atomic replacement of the placeholder. Run `hook_runner(template.hooks(), zettel.get_data(), self.zettelkasten_path)` only after the save returns successfully, preserving today's order. Return the saved `Path`.
+
+Use `finally` cleanup for any exit before save succeeds, including `KeyboardInterrupt`: close any open reservation descriptor and remove only the placeholder owned by this invocation. Compare its original `(st_dev, st_ino)` before unlinking so cleanup cannot delete a file that has replaced it. After `save` returns, retain the note on hook failure. Normalize ordinary hook exceptions with `raise RuntimeError(f"note saved at {path}, but hook failed: {exc}") from exc`; never catch `BaseException` for hook normalization. Never unlink an occupied path whose reservation this invocation lost. Process termination that cannot run `finally` may leave a zero-byte reservation; do not automatically steal it.
+
+### CreateNoteParams and CommandCreateNote
+
+Keep existing fields and append:
+
+```python
+body: str | None = None
+source: Path | None = None
+dry_run: bool = False
+```
+
+The constructor becomes:
+
+```python
+def __init__(
+    self,
+    params: CreateNoteParams,
+    path_zettelkasten: Path,
+    repo: ZettelRepository,
+    templates: dict[str, Any],
+    hook_runner: Any,
+    formatter: ZettelFormatter,
+) -> None: ...
+```
+
+`execute(self) -> CommandResult` remains the shared entry point. Resolve `path_zettelkasten` and derive `vault_root = path_zettelkasten.parent`. Preserve the existing constructor directory check and template question/default behavior.
+
+Before template construction, split `params.tags` on commas; strip each item, remove one leading `#`, lowercase it, drop empty items, and deduplicate in first-occurrence order. Accept only `re.fullmatch(r"[\w-]+(/[\w-]+)*", item)` with no `re.fullmatch(r"[\d/]+", item)`. Thus Unicode word characters, underscores and nesting are accepted; whitespace, repeated `#`, punctuation and purely numeric nesting fail. Return `CommandResult(success=False, error=f"invalid tag '{item}': use letters, digits, '-', '_', and '/' for nesting")` for the cleaned invalid item. Supply the comma-joined normalized string in `answers["tags"]` when tags were explicitly provided; do not add it when `params.tags is None`. Question handling must not overwrite normalized `tags` with an unvalidated answer.
+
+Reject `params.body is not None and params.source is not None` before reading either input. For source input, resolve the path and require an existing regular file, suffix `.md`, and containment under the resolved `<vault_root>/inbox/`. Resolving an inbox symlink must not broaden the allowed vault root; check that the resolved inbox itself remains under `vault_root`. Invalid input returns exactly `--source must be a Markdown file inside <vault_root>/inbox`, replacing `<vault_root>` with its absolute path. Do not import server middleware into the command.
+
+Read source as UTF-8, normalize CRLF, and remove at most one leading frontmatter block matching `r"\A---\n[\s\S]*?\n---\n"`. Use its remaining text as `body`. When `params.title is None`, use the source file stem before the usual title fixers. Do not overwrite an explicit title. After this derivation, missing type or title keeps the existing `zettel_type and title are required` error. An unknown template keeps `Unknown template: <name>`.
+
+For `dry_run=True`, call `use_case.prepare(template, answers, body=body)` only and format its zettel using `PrintZettelUseCase(self.formatter).execute(zettel.get_data())`. No reserve, save, hooks, source move, or trash-directory creation occurs. For a real create, call `use_case.execute(template, answers, body=body)` and read the saved zettel through `repo.find_by_location(str(path))` to build metadata from the final saved data rather than a second independently prepared candidate.
+
+Success metadata is a flat JSON-compatible dictionary:
+
+| Key | Type and value |
+| --- | --- |
+| `id` | `str(zettel.id)` |
+| `type` | saved/prepared zettel type, a string |
+| `title` | saved/prepared zettel title, a string |
+| `tags` | `list[str]`, using `zettel.tags or []` |
+| `path` | absolute resolved path as `str` |
+| `relative_path` | `path.relative_to(vault_root).as_posix()` |
+| `wikilink` | `f"[[{relative_path_without_md}|{title}]]"` |
+| `dry_run` | `True`, present only on dry run |
+| `content` | formatted Markdown string, present only on dry run |
+| `trashed_source` | absolute destination string, present after a completed source move |
+| `errors` | `list[str]`, present when post-save source cleanup has a problem |
+
+For example: `relative_path="notes/20261108134925.md"`, `wikilink="[[notes/20261108134925|Title]]"`. Do not add a `date` field to this payload: compare id/date using the written note's frontmatter in acceptance checks. Real success retains `output=f"Created {path}"`.
+
+After save and metadata readback succeed, move a source into `<vault_root>/.trash/`. Resolve and confine the trash directory beneath the vault before creating it. Try `<name>`, then `<stem> 1<suffix>`, `<stem> 2<suffix>`, up to `MAX_TRASH_ATTEMPTS = 1000` candidates total. On exhaustion retain the source, keep success, append a cleanup error and omit `trashed_source`. Use the existing no-clobber move pattern (`os.link(source, destination)` then `source.unlink()`) so a concurrent destination collision retries a suffix without overwriting data. A link/move failure, including cross-device failure, is post-save: keep `success=True`, keep the note, append the error to metadata `errors`, and omit `trashed_source` unless removal completed. Never remove an existing trash entry. A failed source unlink may leave both files; report their paths.
+

A hook failure preserves the exact `note saved at <path>, but hook failed: <error>` message. Once execute has returned a path, catch ordinary readback or metadata failures separately and report `note saved at <path>, but metadata failed: <error>`. Both failures retain the saved note and source; this explicit path tells scripts to inspect that note instead of blindly retrying. Keep the PRD's failure JSON shape `{"error": message}`. Do not broaden this PRD into a hook transaction redesign.
+
+### CLI and other adapters
+
+Add Click options `--body-file PATH`, `--source PATH`, `--dry-run` and `--json` to `create_note`. Use plain string paths with validation inside the callback, avoiding parse-time `exists=True` checks. `--body-file -` reads text from stdin; other body files are read as UTF-8 and passed in `CreateNoteParams.body`. Pass source paths without reading them in the adapter. Check mutual exclusion before opening a body file or source. In human mode report this through `console.panic`; in JSON mode emit the failure object below and exit 1.
+
+Explicit scripting flags (`--body-file`, `--source`, `--dry-run`, `--json`) select the command path even when required fields are absent, producing a command error rather than starting a TUI. `-t` plus `--source` is sufficient without `--title`. Existing no-flag incomplete invocations retain their TUI behavior. `--list` retains its current human listing; reject combining `--list` with `--json` through the JSON failure path rather than emitting non-JSON lines.
+
+With `--json`, successful create/dry-run prints exactly `json.dumps(result.metadata, ensure_ascii=False)` through `click.echo` plus its final newline. Failure prints exactly `json.dumps({"error": message}, ensure_ascii=False)` through `click.echo` and exits 1. Route callback validation, body-read failures and constructor failures through that same path. Do not call `console.report_result`, success messages, or the TUI in JSON mode. This payload is the PRD's explicit exception to the console-output invariant. Unknown-template output is exactly `{"error": "Unknown template: nonexistent"}` with exit 1.

+Without JSON, real create uses the existing `Created <path>` reporting. Dry run prints metadata `content` with `console.print(mode="raw")`, without a Created line. Place sync's exit outside infrastructure exception conversion. The `query` branch with neither `-Q` nor `-q` reports its existing message and then calls `ctx.exit(1)`. Do not change cancel/confirmation exits or invent a broad interactive-error overhaul.

+The scripting contract is version 1. Its keys and types are stable; future additions are additive and consumers must ignore unknown keys. Removing or retyping a key requires a new contract flag or a major package release. Document this policy and the failure-exit behavior change in the CLI docs, agent skill and changelog; do not add an unrequested schema key.

+## Data flow
+
+1. CLI parses flags and reads body-file/stdin; API/TUI construct the same params. The command validates tags, source confinement and required fields, then gathers template answers.
+2. The use case builds fresh template data, appends normalized body, runs domain fixers, and checks the id path. Collision checks and reservation losses consume one shared five-candidate budget.
+3. Dry run returns the prepared candidate to `PrintZettelUseCase` and returns metadata/content without writes.
+4. Real create exclusively reserves the candidate, atomically saves through the existing repository, runs hooks, and returns `Path`.
+5. The command reads the saved note through the existing repository, derives metadata, and moves a source to recoverable trash. Post-save trash failures remain successful results with `errors`.
+6. The adapter emits the requested representation and maps failed results to exit 1. No library component emits terminal output.

+## Risks & edge cases
+
+- Local ids repeat during DST fall-back and templates can pin dates; five real-clock rebuilds fail safely rather than fabricating a future date. A dry-run id is a preview, never a reservation promise.
+- Exclusive reservations coordinate creators using this protocol. An abrupt kill can leave an empty file; allocation treats it as occupied. Atomic writer replacement changes the placeholder inode, so failed-save cleanup must preserve a completed replacement.
+- Hooks still run after persistence. Existing project hooks mutate in-memory resources after the write; PRD 00119 owns changing that timing. Hook/readback failures can leave a created note and must name that possibility.
+- Source paths and `.trash` can contain symlinks; resolve and check confinement before filesystem operations. Confinement here follows the repo's existing resolved-path policy, not a new descriptor-relative filesystem sandbox.
+- No-clobber hard-link moves can fail across mounted subtrees or filesystems without hard-link support. The note remains successful and the source remains available with a reported cleanup error. A future source-relocation requirement may justify a copy-plus-exclusive-destination fallback.
+- Existing consumers comparing `metadata["path"]` to `Path` need updated expectations: this PRD deliberately makes it a JSON-compatible absolute string.
+- Likely next changes are 00119's vault templates/body-section selection and pre-save hooks, 00120's link resolution, and the create-note skill migration. The optional `body_section` attribute, flat metadata and unchanged public Path return provide those seams without implementing them early.

+        trash.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

+        def record_open(target: Any, flags: int, mode: int = 511, **kwargs: Any) -> int:
+            descriptor = original_open(target, flags, mode, **kwargs)
+            if Path(target) == path:
+                descriptors.append(descriptor)
+            return descriptor
+
+        def fail_inspection(descriptor: int) -> os.stat_result:
+            if descriptor in descriptors:
+                if replace_placeholder and replacement.exists():
+                    replacement.replace(path)
+                raise error
+            return original_fstat(descriptor)
+
+        try:
+            with monkeypatch.context() as boundary:
+                boundary.setattr(os, "open", record_open)

+            assert len(descriptors) == 1

+            with pytest.raises(OSError):

+        def record_open(path: Any, flags: int, mode: int = 511, **kwargs: Any) -> int:
+            descriptor = original_open(path, flags, mode, **kwargs)

# Test Author Prompt (Tess)

Tess writes tests from requirements. She has NOT seen and must NOT think about implementation.

## Prompt Template

The prompt template lives in `work/references/tess-prompt.md` (single source
of truth, registry-shaped single-brace placeholders — `render_prompt.py`
consumes it directly; see `agent-registry.md` for the placeholder table).

## Context Selection

When building Tess's prompt, include:

| Include | Why |
|---------|-----|
| Task description + acceptance criteria | The spec Tess tests against |
| Public types/interfaces | So Tess knows the API surface |
| One sample test file | So Tess follows project conventions |
| Test framework config | So imports and assertions are correct |
| `<dir>/tests/HARNESS_CONTRACT.md`, when it exists | The project's own harness rules, for each Contract path `<dir>/<file>` the task touches |

| Exclude | Why |
|---------|-----|
| Architecture docs | Would leak implementation thinking |
| AGENTS.md internals | Same - Tess doesn't need to know how things are built |
| Implementation files | Defeats the entire purpose |
| "How to build this" guidance | Tess is a test author, not an implementor |

Moved verbatim out of `SKILL.md` step 2.7 (PRD 00119-v2) — the two lists the
step used to spell out inline. **Read this section before the first Tess
dispatch of a batch.**

**Tess receives:**
- Task description and acceptance criteria
- The **exact file paths** the task touches — spelled **absolute** — and the **exact symbol names** to test, taken from the plan task — not "find the relevant file"
- Public interfaces/types relevant to the task
- The project's test-harness contract when one exists (PRD 00141): for each Contract path `<dir>/<file>`, `<dir>/tests/HARNESS_CONTRACT.md` joins the `PUBLIC_INTERFACES` `--set-cmd`, once per distinct file; no such file adds nothing. It carries harness rules, never implementation — a harness can make a test pass for reasons requirements cannot reveal (a `capture_main` that installs its own `sys.stdin`, so a "marker checked before stdin" test passes against the old code too)
- Existing test patterns (one sample test file from the project)
- Test framework and conventions used

**Tess does NOT receive:**
- Implementation strategy or architecture docs (loaded in step 2.5 for the main session and Ivan only)
- "How to build this" context
- Access to modify non-test files

The stdout integer from step 2.7's render call **is** the Subagent Dispatch Budget measurement — no separate `wc -c`. `tess-prompt.md` bakes in the read-only-scope instruction, the dispatch prologue, the Assumptions footer and the size limits (rule 12: functions under 50 lines, files under 800) permanently (mirroring `ivan.md`), so nothing further needs adding to the prompt by hand — open-ended discovery is where subagents burn turns and stall, and keeping Tess scoped to the listed files/symbols is the template's job now. Dispatch the Agent tool with the file at `docs/dev/tmp/dispatch-tess-<task-id>.txt` as the prompt source. The template also embeds Simplicity/Think-Before-Coding/Surgical rules to prevent Tess from writing speculative tests or silently assuming input shape.

## Quality gate (step 2.8)

Moved verbatim out of `SKILL.md` step 2.8 (PRD 00119-v2). SKILL.md keeps the
gate rule and the total-Tess budget; the rubric and the retry render live here.
**Read this section before running the gate on Tess's first test file.**

**Run the computed shape check first**, on every test file Tess wrote or changed:

```bash
python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/review-work-completion/scripts/detect_tautological_tests.py <test file>...
```

It prints one `[MECH] {emoji} <test> <reason> | File: <path>:<line> | Task: general` line per test whose shape cannot fail (a constant or self-comparing assert, an `A or B` hedge, a swallowed exception, `raises(Exception)`, no assertion at all) and always exits 0. **Every `[MECH]` line is a check-4 failure**: copy it verbatim into the `QUALITY_FEEDBACK` file, then judge the four checks below by reading. The script sees shape only; a test that restates the code in a perfectly valid shape is still check 4's to catch by hand. The same script runs at review (`review-work-completion` step 3), so a shape that slips past here comes back as a `mech-check` finding and a rework cycle — cheaper to fix now.

Before committing Tess's tests, review them in the main session against this checklist:

1. **Behavior names?** Each test name describes a behavior ("rejects empty email"), not an implementation detail ("calls validateEmail")
2. **Real assertions?** Assertions check outputs/effects, not mock internals
3. **Edge cases?** Empty, null, boundary, error, and concurrent cases covered where relevant
4. **No tautologies?** Tests don't just restate what the code obviously does
5. **Exploit classes covered?** Every tested function has the six rule-6a assertions (two fixture values per asserted field, a near-miss negative, a multi-element and an empty input, an accept and a reject case of the same shape, a surfaced error, a dependency assertion); a missing one is a check-5 failure and names the class.

If any check fails, dispatch Tess again with specific feedback about what's weak. Render the retry the same way as the initial dispatch — never author it by hand:

```bash
python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/scripts/render_prompt.py ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/references/tess-retry-prompt.md \
  --out docs/dev/tmp/dispatch-tess-<task-id>-retry-<n>.txt \
  --set-file QUALITY_FEEDBACK=docs/dev/tmp/tess-<task-id>-gate-<n>.txt \
  --set-file TASK_DESCRIPTION=<the same scratch file step 2.7 used> \
  --set-file TASK_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA=docs/dev/tmp/tess-<task-id>-acceptance.txt --dispatch-kind tess --dispatch-task <task-id>
```

Write the gate findings (one per line) to the `QUALITY_FEEDBACK` scratch file with the Write tool. Max 2 quality gate retries.

### Style limits on the test files

Once the four checks pass, run the step-5.65 gate over the test files only, so an oversized test file is split by a Tess retry now (cheap, tests-only) instead of an Ivan style-fix dispatch after implementation (PRD 00197; `tess-prompt.md` rule 12 already tells her the limits). Build the diff the way `references/style-gate.md` § Diff construction does, over this task's test files alone: `git diff <task_base_sha> --output=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/test-diff-<task-id>.txt -- <tracked test files>` (`--output=` goes before `--`; after it git reads it as a pathspec and prints the diff to stdout instead), then `git diff --no-index -- /dev/null <file> >> ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/test-diff-<task-id>.txt` per untracked test file (exit 1 is the normal case; only exit ≥2 is a failure), then `mv ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/test-diff-<task-id>.txt docs/dev/tmp/test-diff-<task-id>.txt`. Then:

```bash
python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/scripts/check_style_limits.py --diff docs/dev/tmp/test-diff-<task-id>.txt <each new or changed test file as an absolute path>
```

Exit 0 is clean. Exit 1 is a quality-gate failure: write the violation lines to the `QUALITY_FEEDBACK` scratch file and render the retry above; it counts toward the two quality-gate retries. Exit 2 (the script could not run) is not a Tess failure: name it in the task output and proceed, step 5.65 measures the same files again after implementation.

## Retry Prompt (after quality gate failure)

The retry template lives in `work/references/tess-retry-prompt.md` (single
source of truth, registry-shaped single-brace placeholders — `render_prompt.py`
consumes it directly; see `agent-registry.md` for the placeholder table). It
takes `{QUALITY_FEEDBACK}`, `{TASK_DESCRIPTION}` and
`{TASK_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA}`, and bakes in the same fixed guards the initial
template carries (read-only scope, 100K abort line, dispatch prologue,
ASSUMPTIONS footer).

`{QUALITY_FEEDBACK}` is the step-2.8 gate's own findings, one per line, e.g.:

- Test "handles validation" is too vague. Name the specific behavior.
- Test 3 would pass with a function that always returns true. Add constraints.
- No edge case for empty input.

# Per-Task Review Mechanics (step 5.7)

Moved verbatim out of `SKILL.md` step 5.7 (PRD 00119-v2; situational: consulted
once the tier gate says a task IS reviewed). SKILL.md keeps the tier-gate table,
the `pat.md` render block and the MEDIUM-retry rule; this file owns the runner
dispatch and the result-handling ladder. **Read it before the first step-5.7
dispatch of a batch.**

## Why the lane is tier-gated

A `haiku`-tier task commits after per-task test verification (step 5.5) with **no** review dispatch and proceeds straight to step 6 — it relies on per-task test verification plus the mandated PRD-level review lenses (consensus, blind, doubt — every review cycle reviews every task's diff regardless of tier). The reviewer is a fixed-model helper-script lane (Sonnet via `use-sonnet`) — reviewer capability is deliberately independent of the task's implementor tier. (Why tier-gated: `references/design-rationale.md` § tier-gated pipeline.)

## Test-only diffs

Before anything below, SKILL.md step 5.7 applies `test_only_gate` (from
`skills/work/scripts/work_routing.py`) to
`git diff --name-only <task_base_sha>..HEAD`. When every changed path is test or
fixture code and the task is **not** in rework mode, the whole step is skipped:
no render, no dispatch, `review: "skipped:test-only"` on the attempt record and
in the phase report. Every tier takes the skip, `fable` included.
`dev/bin/release-checks`'s own registration line counts as test code here
too, but only alongside a real test file in the same diff — a diff touching
`dev/bin/release-checks` alone is never test-only.

A rework task keeps its reviewer even on a test-only diff — its CLOSURE verdicts
are what end the review cycle, so skipping him would leave nothing to close on.
One production path anywhere in the diff runs this file in full.

## Recorded verification

Pat is dispatched with no tools, so he cannot run the tests himself. Before the
render, write `docs/dev/tmp/review-task-<id>-verification.txt` with the **Write
tool** (never a shell redirect — command output carries quotes and newlines):
the exact command(s) step 5.5 ran, each exit code, and the runner's own summary
line (for example `12 passed in 0.4s`). When step 5.5 could not run, write the
attempt's literal `verification: skipped:<cause>` value instead. That file is
what `--set-file VERIFICATION_RESULT=` reads, and it is the only test evidence
Pat has.

## Dispatch

Dispatch via the sonnet runner (helper-script dispatch — the **Subagent Watchdog** applies), after SKILL.md step 5.7's render call has written the prompt file:

```bash
bash ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/use-sonnet/scripts/sonnet-run.sh -t "" -S "<pat_session_id>" -f docs/dev/tmp/review-task-<id>-prompt.md -o docs/dev/tmp/review-task-<id>.md
```

Run it as a plain foreground Bash call (the Bash tool's `timeout`, 600000 ms,
the tool's maximum, bounds it), never with `run_in_background`. A headless loop session that ends
its turn while a background job is still running is torn down together with
the job: the output file reads `[killed]`, Pat's dispatch row reads `lost`, and
the wrapper relaunches a session that re-orients and re-runs him (2026-09-14,
00191 T1 and agent-skills 00052 T2, one session lost each). If a run was
backgrounded anyway, the next call is `Monitor` on its output file, never a
bare end of turn.

`-t ""` grants the child no tools at all: Pat judges the diff, the task text and
the recorded verification, and nothing else. No `-a`/`-y` either — the reviewer
needs no write access, and a read-only dispatch must never run with bypassed
permissions.

`-S "<pat_session_id>"` (step 5.7 item 1) fixes this conversation's id so a later
cycle can resume it. Everything else about the first dispatch is unchanged, and
when no id could be generated the flag is simply dropped.

## Delta re-runs

Every cycle after the first resumes the conversation that raised the findings
instead of starting over. Pat already read `<task_base_sha>..<last_reviewed_sha>`;
re-sending it is what made a second dispatch cost a whole task diff — a measured
369 KB prompt, sent twice, to check a one-file fix.

**Check the delta is non-empty first.** An empty `git diff <last_reviewed_sha>..HEAD`
means the fix never committed, and `render_prompt.py` exits 4 on a `--set-cmd`
that produces no output. Do not dispatch: there is nothing new to judge, the
previous cycle's findings stand, and the loop continues through the CRITICAL/HIGH
row below whose 3-cycle cap is what ends it.

For cycle `<n>` (2 or 3):

1. Write the findings you sent the fixer, verbatim, one per line, to
   `docs/dev/tmp/review-task-<id>-prior-<n>.txt` with the **Write tool**. A
   finding line carries backticks and pipes, so it never crosses the shell as a
   `--set` word.
2. Render the re-run prompt:

   ```bash
   python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/scripts/render_prompt.py ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/references/pat-rerun-prompt.md \
     --out docs/dev/tmp/review-task-<id>-rerun-<n>.md \
     --set-file PRIOR_FINDINGS=docs/dev/tmp/review-task-<id>-prior-<n>.txt \
     --set-cmd DELTA_DIFF="git diff <last_reviewed_sha>..HEAD" \
     --set UNCHANGED_NOTE="You already reviewed <task_base_sha>..<last_reviewed_sha> earlier in this conversation. That range is unchanged and is not repeated here." --dispatch-kind pat --dispatch-task <id>
   ```

3. Dispatch it with `-R` where the first dispatch had `-S`, same output file:

   ```bash
   bash ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/use-sonnet/scripts/sonnet-run.sh -t "" -R "<pat_session_id>" -f docs/dev/tmp/review-task-<id>-rerun-<n>.md -o docs/dev/tmp/review-task-<id>.md
   ```

4. Advance `<last_reviewed_sha>` to the HEAD this dispatch just read, so cycle
   3's delta is cycle 2's fix alone and never the accumulated range.

The reply goes through the same `parse_review.py` gate and the same ladder below:
the reporting contract is unchanged, so nothing downstream cares that the prompt
was a delta. A correction retry (exit 1) re-renders `pat.md`, not this template —
a reply that broke the line shape is not a resume problem.

**No `<pat_session_id>` means no delta lane at all.** When step 5.7 could not
generate an id, or § Resume failure dropped it, every cycle takes the full-diff
dispatch of § Dispatch with neither `-S` nor `-R` — exactly today's behavior.
Never dispatch `-R ""`.

## Resume failure

A `-R` dispatch that exits non-zero or leaves the output file empty (a session
that no longer resolves exits 1 with `No conversation found with session ID:`)
re-dispatches **once** with today's full-diff prompt: re-render `pat.md` exactly
as SKILL.md step 5.7 item 2 does, with `--set-cmd DIFF="git diff <task_base_sha>..HEAD"`,
and run the § Dispatch command above with neither `-S` nor `-R`. Record
`resume_failed` on the attempt record's `review` field (`references/attempt-logging.md`
§ `review` for the shape) and name the fallback in the phase report — a cheap
review that silently did not happen is worse than an expensive one that did.

Then **drop `<pat_session_id>`** and advance `<last_reviewed_sha>` to the HEAD
that fallback read. The session is gone; leaving the id in place would aim every
remaining cycle at a `-R` that is already known to fail, spending a doomed
dispatch each time.

That is the same single retry the runner-failure row below grants, not an extra
one: a second failure takes that row's `review: failed:<cause>` path.

## Result handling

**Validate the reply first.** Every read of the output file, including each
re-run inside the ladder below, goes through the parser:

```bash
python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/scripts/parse_review.py docs/dev/tmp/review-task-<id>.md
```

- **Exit 0** — the JSON on stdout (`no_findings`, `findings`, `closures`) is what
  the ladder below reads. Do not re-parse the raw text by hand.
- **Exit 1** — the reply broke the reporting contract. Write this text verbatim
  to `docs/dev/tmp/review-task-<id>-correction.txt` with the **Write tool**,
  re-render `pat.md` with every flag identical except
  `--set-file CONTRACT_CORRECTION=docs/dev/tmp/review-task-<id>-correction.txt`,
  then dispatch **once** more — with `-R "<pat_session_id>"`, never `-S`. The
  session already exists by then, and re-passing `-S` with the same id exits 1
  on `Error: Session ID <id> is already in use.` (verified live 2026-08-28),
  which would spend the whole correction retry on a runner failure. No id in
  hand → neither flag. A `-R` that fails here takes § Resume failure:

  > Your previous reply did not follow the reporting contract. Reply again with only lines of the form `SEVERITY | file:line | issue | fix` (CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW), CLOSURE lines where the description carries a findings block, or the single line `NO FINDINGS`. No other text.

  **Never `--set` this one.** The text carries backticks; inside a double-quoted
  Bash word they are command substitution, so the correction would reach the
  reviewer with the line shapes it is teaching replaced by empty strings — on
  the single dispatch whose whole job is teaching the line shape. Same rule as
  the task-authored prose flags, and for the same reason.

  A second exit 1 records `review: "failed:invalid_output"` on the attempt
  record and in the phase report (fail loud), then proceeds to step 6. The
  mandatory PRD-level review catches what Pat missed. There is no third
  dispatch.
- **Exit 2** — the output file is missing or empty. That is the runner-failure
  row at the bottom of this list, not a contract failure.

Then handle the parsed result:

- **`CLOSURE | resolved|unresolved | ...` verdicts** (rework tasks only — the persona emits one per finding when the task description carries a `### Findings (verbatim)` block, per PRD 00095). A `resolved` verdict needs nothing. **Treat every `unresolved` verdict as a HIGH finding** and run it through the same loop as the row below: verify it against the code first, then dispatch Ivan with the confirmed gap. This exists because "the diff looks fine" and "the reported defect is gone" are different questions, and the review that answered only the first let a task ship with `_run_status` still swallowing `FileNotFoundError` while its review read "fixed inline". Step 5.5 already covers findings that produced a test; these verdicts are what closes the ones that did not.
- **CRITICAL or HIGH findings** — treat like a failed verification: verify each finding against the code first and discard wrong ones (the reviewer can be wrong), then re-render `ivan.md` using the full retry command shape in `references/gate-failure.md` § Retry render, writing the confirmed findings to the `FAILING_TESTS` scratch file and passing `--set RETRY_INSTRUCTION="Apply ONLY the specific fixes listed below. Do not refactor surrounding code or address unrelated issues you notice."`. The code-quality rules block is already permanent in `ivan.md` — do not re-include it. Re-commit (step 5), re-verify (step 5.5), re-review through § Delta re-runs. Max 3 review cycles, then proceed with warning.
- **MEDIUM outside this task's files, LOW only, or `NO FINDINGS`** - note them in the task output, proceed to step 6.
- **Runner unavailable, exit nonzero, or output file missing/empty** — retry ONCE. On the second failure: record `review: failed:<cause>` in the task's attempt entry and the phase report (fail loud), then proceed to step 6 — the reviewer lane never blocks the batch; the PRD-level review lenses catch what it missed.

The MEDIUM-inside-this-task's-files row stays in `SKILL.md` step 5.7: it is the
one branch a passing review still has to stamp on the attempt record.

# Attempt Logging

At every task exit — success in `SKILL.md` step 6, abort in step 4 (timeout / context exceeded / error after debug), or via the Subagent Dispatch Budget overrun path — append one entry to `state.tasks[i].attempts[]`. Under in-loop escalation (PRD 00065) a task can run at more than one rung: each rung that dispatched writes its own entry, at exit or when the task escalates away from it — see Cardinality below.

```json
{
  "attempt": <len(existing attempts) + 1>,
  "model": "<tier>",
  "outcome": "completed" | "aborted" | "escalated",
  "review_cycle": <int | null>,
  "cause": "<string | null>",
  "implementor": "claude" | "gemini" | "qwen" | "codex" | "orchestrator",
  "preflight_outcome": "healthy" | "pi_missing" | "endpoint_unreachable" | "model_id_missing" | "completion_failed" | null,
  "pipeline": "minimal" | "lean" | "full",
  "escalation_reason": "gate_failure" | "review_flag" | null,
  "escalated_from": "qwen" | "codex" | "haiku" | "sonnet" | "opus" | null,
  "diagnosis": "spec_gap" | "solid_spec" | null,
  "repair_used": true | null,
  "breaker_skipped": true | null,
  "qwen_excluded_reason": "files" | "memory_pressure" | "memory_probe_failed" | null,
  "qwen_gate_failed": true | null,
  "codex_no_edit": true | null,
  "codex_no_edit_probe_exit": <int | null>,
  "verification": "skipped:<cause>" | "timeout:<command>" | null,
  "red_check": "skipped:<cause>" | "n/a:new_module" | "n/a:test-only-task" | "n/a:docs-only-task" | "n/a:config-only-task" | "n/a:micro-lane" | null,
  "self_deslop": "committed:<sha>" | "noop" | "skipped:trivial" | "skipped:test-only" | "timeout" | "errored:<cause>" | null,
  "style_gate": "clean" | "fixed:<sha>" | "failed:<detail>" | "skipped:tier" | null,
  "devon": "skipped:prose" | "exploit_fixed" | null,
  "devon_exploit": <string | null>,
  "devon_weak_points": <int | null>,
  "devon_in_contract": [<string>] | null,
  "split_hygiene": "clean" | "fixed:<sha>" | "failed:<detail>" | "skipped:no-tests" | null,
  "micro_lane": "overrun" | null,
  "reflow": "<path>:<hunks>" | null,
  "review": "failed:<cause>" | "failed:invalid_output" | "skipped:test-only" | "resume_failed" | null
}
```

**Timing is deliberately not an attempt field.** No timestamp, duration or prompt size is stamped here: an attempt spans several dispatches — Tess, Ivan, Pat and their retries — so one pair of stamps could not say which of them took the hour. Those live in the dispatch ledger, `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/dispatch-metrics.jsonl` (a start row and one or more end rows per dispatch, joined on `id`, plus one row per session-handoff edge; `references/subagent-dispatch.md` § Dispatch telemetry), and a task's runtime is read from its rows there, keyed on `task`.

**Cardinality (PRD 00065)**: today `/autopilot:work` appends exactly one entry per task at exit. Under in-loop escalation the rule widens to one entry per rung/dispatch-group: each rung that dispatched writes its own entry when the task escalates away from it or exits on it. `attempt` numbers stay sequential across rungs (`len(existing)+1`). This is a widening, not a break — a task that never escalates still writes exactly one entry, byte-identical to today.

**Field semantics**:

- `attempt`: 1-indexed; `len(existing) + 1`.
- `model`: the tier `/autopilot:work` used for this pass. Read from `state.tasks[i].model` when set. On legacy plans where `state.tasks[i].model` is absent, record the effective session-inherited tier as a string (e.g. `"sonnet"` for a Work-phase Sonnet 4.6 launch). Always a string — never `null`.
- `outcome`: `/autopilot:work` writes `"completed"`, `"aborted"`, or `"escalated"`. The `"escalated"` value (PRD 00065) is stamped on the entry for a rung the task was reset away from and escalated up; the final rung's entry carries the real terminal outcome (`completed`/`aborted`), and the escalated-away entry keeps its true `implementor` (a qwen rung escalated to Sonnet keeps `implementor:"qwen"`). Later phases upgrade earlier entries — `/autopilot:run-autopilot` Phase 6 (Rework) step 2 rewrites a `"completed"` entry's outcome to `"review_flagged"` at the start of escalation, then later rewrites a flagged entry's outcome to `"rework_failed"` when the rework pass also fails at the top of the chain.
- `review_cycle`: `null` on a first/Phase-3 attempt; set to the current `state.cycle` integer when the pass is a rework re-dispatch (see `SKILL.md` step 1.5 "Rework-mode task filter (PRD 00025)").
- `cause`: `null` on success; on abort or output rejection, the reason — `"context_overrun"`, `"subagent_prompt_overrun"`, `"timeout"`, `"error"`, `"subagent_infra_failure"`, `"commit_rejected"` (a commit blocked by `validate_commit_msg`/warden that the one-retry repair could not fix — `SKILL.md` step 5), `"codex_no_edit"` (PRD 00077; the no-edit infra arm, stamped when the codex helper exited 0 with a non-empty output file but produced no working-tree change — the hook-blocked, prose-only case; classified as INFRA, so the attempt falls back to Claude at the task's own tier with no `escalation_reason` stamp). Qwen output rejections use `"qwen_no_edit"` (no task-owned implementation diff) or `"qwen_test_mutation"` (Tess tests differ from their test commit), with `outcome: "escalated"` on the rejected Qwen row; both are capability failures before staging/gating, never infra.
- `implementor`: which agent actually ran the attempt — `"claude"` (Agent dispatch at any Claude tier, including a Claude fallback when qwen preflight failed), `"gemini"` (UI task via `use-gemini` helper), `"qwen"` (backend qwen-eligible task with healthy preflight, dispatched via `use-qwen` helper), `"codex"` (a codex-eligible backend task the step-3 interception routed to the codex rung, dispatched via the `use-codex` helper), or `"orchestrator"` (PRD 00148; a rework task the micro lane kept in-session — the orchestrator edited it with the Edit tool and no implementor subagent dispatched at all). Sourced from the routing decision in `work` SKILL.md step 3 — the value reflects what dispatched, not what the routing table initially picked: a qwen-eligible task that preflight-failed and fell back to Claude records `"claude"`; likewise, a codex-eligible task whose batch health probe came back unhealthy and fell back to Claude records `"claude"`, not `"codex"`. **Multi-implementor pass (qwen → Claude retry):** under default escalation, each rung writes its own entry: the rejected Qwen row stays `implementor: "qwen"`, `outcome: "escalated"`, and the Sonnet row records `implementor: "claude"`, `escalation_reason: "gate_failure"`, `escalated_from: "qwen"`. This also applies to pre-commit output rejections under `legacy`, which must retain their failure cause. The old single task-exit row applies only to legacy test-gate retries that committed Qwen code, not output rejections. Tess / Devon / code reviewer dispatches do not write attempt entries themselves; this field labels the Ivan-implementor pass.
- `preflight_outcome`: only meaningful for attempts on qwen-eligible tasks (those whose effective eligibility remains true after write-set reconciliation). For qwen-eligible attempts: one of `"healthy"`, `"pi_missing"`, `"endpoint_unreachable"`, `"model_id_missing"`, `"completion_failed"` — the verdict of the four-check probe defined in `references/qwen-integration.md` (Preflight section). For non-qwen-eligible attempts: `null`. A qwen-eligible attempt that the breaker (row 3) or the memory-pressure gate (row 4) rerouted also records `null`, because the probe never ran. Sourced from the preflight probe in `work` SKILL.md step 3.
- `pipeline`: which pipeline depth this attempt ran, keyed on the task tier (PRD 00044) — `"minimal"` (haiku: Tess + Ivan, 2 subagents), `"lean"` (sonnet: + step-5.7 reviewer, 3 subagents), or `"full"` (opus: + Devon at step 2.9, 4 subagents). Mapped from `state.tasks[i].model`: `haiku` → `"minimal"`, `sonnet` → `"lean"`, `opus` → `"full"`; absent/legacy `state.tasks[i].model` is treated as `sonnet` → `"lean"` (matching the step-2.9 and step-5.7 tier gates). Written at every task exit alongside `implementor`. A Phase-6 escalation to `opus` therefore records `"full"` for the rework attempt. Always a string — never `null`. **In-loop escalation (PRD 00065):** an escalation re-dispatches the implementor for the higher rung and re-runs the tier-appropriate post-implementor gates (step 5.7 reviewer for sonnet+, plus the step-5.5 gate); Devon (step 2.9, pre-implementation adversarial tests) is NOT re-run mid-task. So an in-loop opus escalation stamps `pipeline:"lean"` (implementor+reviewer), reserving `"full"` for a from-scratch opus task/rework that actually ran Devon.
- `escalation_reason` (PRD 00065): string?; `"gate_failure"` stamped directly by `/autopilot:work` on the entry of the rung it escalated INTO (in-loop diagnosis). `"review_flag"` reaches the entry a different way: phase-review Phase 6 writes it (with `escalated_from`) into `state.tasks[i]` via `task-set-meta`, and `/autopilot:work`'s attempt write copies both from `state.tasks[i]` onto the rework entry (`SKILL.md` step 6 point 1 / step 1.5) — the task entry is the carrier, the copy is the wiring. Compound path: if that review-flagged rung then escalates in-loop, the copy happens at `SKILL.md` step 5.5 ESCALATE point 2 (onto the escalate-away entry) and `state.tasks[i]`'s `escalation_reason`/`escalated_from` are cleared at point 3, so the higher in-loop rung records its own `gate_failure` (not a leaked `review_flag`). Absent = neither (legacy / no escalation).
- `escalated_from` (PRD 00065): string?; a tier (`"qwen"`|`"codex"`|`"haiku"`|`"sonnet"`|`"opus"`) — on the entry of the rung escalated INTO, the immediate-prior rung it came from. Set directly by `/autopilot:work` on the in-loop `gate_failure` path; carried from `state.tasks[i]` (as above) on the `review_flag` path. Absent on non-escalated entries.
- `diagnosis` (PRD 00065): string?; `"spec_gap"`|`"solid_spec"` — the 2nd-failure diagnosis verdict, stamped on the entry of the rung that was diagnosed.
- `repair_used` (PRD 00065): bool?; `true` stamped on the entry of the same-tier attempt that ran after a task-description repair; absent otherwise (never written `false`).
- `breaker_skipped` (PRD 00065): bool?; `true` stamped on a qwen-eligible attempt the breaker rerouted off qwen — to codex (PRD 00077) or to Claude at original tier (no preflight probe). Absent otherwise.
- `qwen_excluded_reason` (PRD 00075): string?; `"memory_pressure"` (row 4's `check_memory_pressure.py` exited 1) or `"memory_probe_failed"` (exited 2) — stamped on the entry when `work` SKILL.md step 3 row 4 fired; or `"files"` when runtime write-set reconciliation excludes Qwen; key omitted otherwise. This is an attempt-scoped RUNTIME field, distinct from the plan-time `state.tasks[i].qwen_excluded_reason` (`"ui"`/`"tier"`/`"files"`/`"contract"`) that `/autopilot:plan-tasks` writes — `/autopilot:work` never rewrites planner metadata. Absent on every attempt written before PRD 00075; readers treat absence as "no runtime exclusion", never an error — the same absence tolerance the neighbouring PRD-00065 fields (`breaker_skipped`, `qwen_gate_failed`) get.
- `qwen_gate_failed` (PRD 00065): bool?; `true` stamped on an `implementor:"qwen"` entry whose pre-commit output guard or step-5.5 gate FAILED — the durable signal the qwen capability breaker keys on. Absent otherwise.
- `codex_no_edit` (PRD 00077): bool?; the LATCHED detector result, captured at the dispatch boundary (`work/SKILL.md` step 4, before step 5's `git add`) by comparing the task's own file-slice porcelain before and after the codex dispatch; step 5.5 reads the latched flag and never re-runs the detector. Absent on non-codex attempts and on attempts written before PRD 00077.
- `codex_no_edit_probe_exit` (PRD 00077): int?; the detector's own exit code, recorded ONLY when the detector exited non-zero — a non-zero exit means the probe is INDETERMINATE, not "no change": `codex_no_edit` is NOT latched and the attempt continues on the capability path normally. Exists so a broken detector is visible in the record instead of silently reclassifying every real codex capability failure as infra. Absent when the detector ran cleanly and on attempts written before PRD 00077.

**Best-effort gate stamps (fail-loud markers, PRD 00084 R2d)**: each records that a per-task gate was skipped or failed rather than passed, so a skipped check never reads as a passed one (`rules/operating-principles.md`). All optional — absent means the gate ran normally (or its tier-skip applied). They are pass-through markers: none blocks the task or changes `outcome`.

- `verification`: string?; `"skipped:<cause>"` when step 5.5's per-task test verification could not run (e.g. the build lock was contended and cargo was backgrounded — `SKILL.md` step 5.5 / the "test verification is blocked" rule), or `"timeout:<command>"` (PRD 00167) when step 5.5's narrow tests hit their 300000 ms Bash `timeout` budget and then hit the 600000 ms re-run too, leaving no verdict (`references/subagent-dispatch.md` § Foreground command budgets). `<command>` is the command that timed out, so the record says which one. Two neighbouring timeouts are recorded elsewhere and never here: a step-2.95 red-check takes `red_check: "skipped:<cause>"` from its own ladder (`references/red-check.md`), and step 7's suite runs after every attempt entry is written, so its timeout is recorded in the phase report (`references/final-verification.md` § Timed-out commands). The two values are deliberately distinct: `skipped:` means the check was never attempted, `timeout:` means it was attempted and returned no verdict. Absent when the task's tests ran.
- `red_check`: string?; `"skipped:<cause>"` when step 2.95's red-check could not run standalone (tests import the not-yet-built feature, or the runner cannot execute them), or `"n/a:new_module"` when the check was inapplicable because a Contract-named target the tests import does not exist on disk yet — a module that cannot be imported can only fail with `ImportError`, which proves nothing, so step 2.95 records this and skips both pytest invocations. Or one of `"n/a:test-only-task"`, `"n/a:docs-only-task"`, `"n/a:config-only-task"` (PRD 00141) when step 2.7 skipped Tess for that task class, or `"n/a:micro-lane"` (PRD 00148) when the micro lane skipped steps 2.7-2.95 outright, so step 2.95 has no newly committed tests to run — the value names WHICH class, because the three take different downstream paths (a test-only task still reaches step 5.7's gate, where PRD 00159 skips Pat outside rework mode and stamps `review: "skipped:test-only"`; docs-only and config-only never reach it). The two families are deliberately distinct: `skipped:` means the check could not be run, `n/a:` means it had no signal to give. Absent when the red-check ran (saw red, or strengthened-then-red).
- `self_deslop`: string?; the step-5.6 self-deslop outcome — `"committed:<sha>"` (a `chore: prune slop` cleanup landed), `"noop"` (ran, no slop), `"skipped:trivial"` (skip rule fired — diff <30 net lines OR <2 files), `"skipped:test-only"` (PRD 00159; every path in `<task_base_sha>..HEAD` is test or fixture code, so the pass was never dispatched — a distinct value from `"skipped:trivial"` because the two skips answer different questions and a batch needs to tell them apart), `"timeout"` (watchdog killed it), or `"errored:<cause>"` (dispatch failed). Canonical shape mirrored in `run-autopilot/references/state-schema.md` `tasks[].attempts[].self_deslop`. Absent on legacy attempts.
- `style_gate` (PRD 00163): string?; the step-5.65 style-limit verdict for this task's own diff — `"clean"` (the gate passed, or the task's diff held no `.py` file to measure), `"fixed:<sha>"` (it exited 1, one fix dispatch landed, and the re-run was clean), `"failed:<detail>"` (`<detail>` is the violation lines joined by `"; "` when the re-run still exited 1, or the script's stderr when the gate could not run at all), or `"skipped:tier"` (a `haiku` task, the one tier that skips it). Held in-session and written into step 6's `task-done` payload, the same rule `self_deslop` follows. Absent on legacy attempts and on every attempt written before this PRD, when the gate ran once per phase and stamped nothing per task.
- `split_hygiene` (PRD 00166): string?; the step-5.65 split-hygiene verdict on the test files this task touched — `"clean"` (the check passed), `"fixed:<sha>"` (it exited 1, one deletion-only fix dispatch landed, and the re-run was clean), `"failed:<detail>"` (`<detail>` is the reported lines joined by `"; "` when the re-run still exited 1, or the script's stderr when the check could not run at all), or `"skipped:no-tests"` (the task's candidate list held no test path, so `check_split_hygiene.py` was never invoked). It is a separate field from `style_gate` on purpose: the two run in the same step but answer different questions over different file sets — line spans across every `.py` file versus bindings inside test files — so one verdict can never stand in for the other. Held in-session and written into step 6's `task-done` payload, the same rule `style_gate` follows. Absent on legacy attempts and when the step's haiku tier-gate skipped it.
- `devon` (finding 16, 2026-09-20): string?; `"skipped:prose"` when step 2.9's prose gate skipped Devon because every test file Tess created or changed for the task has a basename ending in `_prose.py` (a substring pin cannot see negation, inversion or past-tense narration, so a Devon round on such a task keeps nothing), or `"exploit_fixed"` when Devon broke the tests, Tess strengthened them once, and the task proceeded on the strengthened tests (no second Devon dispatch). Held in-session and written into step 6's `task-done` payload, the same rule `style_gate` follows. Absent when Devon ran clean or when the tier gate skipped him. Mirror in `run-autopilot/references/state-schema.md` already documents `devon`/`devon_weak_points`/`devon_in_contract`.
- `devon_exploit`: string?; Devon's one-line weak-point summary, stamped alongside `devon: "exploit_fixed"`. Absent otherwise.
- `devon_weak_points`: int?; the count of weak points Devon's numbered `Weak points:` list named, stamped alongside `devon: "exploit_fixed"`. Absent otherwise.
- `devon_in_contract`: string[]?; each `"N. in-contract: ..."` line Tess returned when answering Devon's weak points, stamped alongside `devon: "exploit_fixed"`. Absent otherwise.
- `micro_lane` (PRD 00148): string?; `"overrun"` stamped when the micro lane's post-edit ceiling fired (`net_lines >= 30` OR `file_count > 2`), the edit was reverted with `git checkout --`, and the task fell through to the normal lane at step 2.7 — so the record shows the shortcut was tried and abandoned, not that the task was always normal. - `reflow` (PRD 00148): string?; `"<path>:<hunks>"` (`;`-joined for several) when step 5's `check_reflow.py` flagged a staged file at or above the hunk threshold, or `"failed:<stderr>"` when the script exited 2.
